title.en: Volume 151 Biographies 101: Gao Congwen, Yi Shen, Zhu Zhongliang, Liu Changyi, Fan Xichao, Wan Ge, Yan Juyuan, Meng Yuanyang, Zhao Chang

sentences.zh: 穆寧穆寧，懷州河內人也。

translations.literal: Mu Ning—Mu Ning—was a native of Henei in Huai Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Mu Ning was a native of Henei in Huai Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 父元休，以文學著。

translations.literal: His father Yuanxiu was renowned for literary scholarship.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yuanxiu had earned a reputation for literary learning.

sentences.zh: 撰《洪範外傳》十篇，開元中獻之。

translations.literal: He composed ten chapters of the Supplement to the Great Plan and presented them during the Kaiyuan era.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote ten chapters of the Supplement to the Great Plan and submitted them to the throne during Kaiyuan.

sentences.zh: 玄宗賜帛，授偃師縣丞、安陽令。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanzong rewarded him with silk and appointed him Assistant Magistrate of Yanshi County and Magistrate of Anyang.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanzong granted him silk and appointed him assistant magistrate of Yanshi and magistrate of Anyang.

sentences.zh: 寧清慎剛正，重交遊，以氣節自任。

translations.literal: Ning was pure, cautious, upright, and firm; he valued friendship and held himself to moral resolve.
translations.idiomatic: Ning was scrupulous, cautious, and upright; he prized friendship and measured himself by his integrity.

sentences.zh: 少以明經調授鹽山尉。

translations.literal: In his youth he passed the Mingjing examination and was assigned as district commander of Yanshan.
translations.idiomatic: As a young man he passed the Classics examination and was posted as district commander of Yanshan.

sentences.zh: 是時，安祿山始叛，偽署劉道玄為景城守，寧唱義起兵，斬道玄首。

translations.literal: At that time An Lushan had just rebelled and falsely appointed Liu Daoxuan prefect of Jingcheng; Ning raised troops in righteous cause and beheaded Daoxuan.
translations.idiomatic: An Lushan had just risen in rebellion and installed Liu Daoxuan as prefect of Jingcheng; Ning rallied loyal forces, took up arms, and cut off Daoxuan's head.

sentences.zh: 傳檄郡邑，多有應者。

translations.literal: He circulated proclamations through the commanderies and districts, and many responded.
translations.idiomatic: When he issued his call to arms across the region, many districts answered.

sentences.zh: 賊將史思明來寇郡，寧以攝東光令將兵禦之。

translations.literal: The rebel general Shi Siming came to attack the commandery; Ning, acting as magistrate of Dongguang, led troops to resist him.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebel general Shi Siming invaded the commandery, Ning, serving as acting magistrate of Dongguang, led the defense.

sentences.zh: 思明遣使說誘，寧立斬之。

translations.literal: Siming sent envoys to persuade and entice him; Ning immediately beheaded them.
translations.idiomatic: Siming sent envoys to win him over; Ning had them executed on the spot.

sentences.zh: 郡懼賊怨深，後大兵至，奪寧兵及攝縣。

translations.literal: The commandery feared deep rebel resentment; when a large force later arrived, it stripped Ning of his troops and his acting magistracy.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing that the rebels' wrath would fall heavily on them, the commandery authorities later, when reinforcements arrived, stripped Ning of his troops and his acting post.

sentences.zh: 初，寧佐采訪使巡按，常過平原，與太守顏真卿密揣祿山必叛。

translations.literal: Earlier, while assisting a regional inspector on circuit, Ning often passed through Pingyuan and with the prefect Yan Zhenqing privately judged that Lushan would surely rebel.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, while serving an assistant to a regional inspector on tour, he often visited Pingyuan and confided in the prefect Yan Zhenqing that Lushan was certain to rebel.

sentences.zh: 至是，真卿亦唱義，舉郡兵以拒祿山。

translations.literal: At this juncture Zhenqing also raised troops in righteous cause and mustered the commandery's forces to resist Lushan.
translations.idiomatic: Now Zhenqing too took up the loyal cause and raised the commandery's troops against Lushan.

sentences.zh: 會間使持書遺真卿曰：「夫子為衛君乎？」

translations.literal: By chance a secret messenger brought a letter to Zhenqing saying, "Will the Master serve as ruler of Wei?"
translations.idiomatic: A secret courier then brought Zhenqing a letter that read only, "Will the Master serve as ruler of Wei?

sentences.zh: 更無他詞。

translations.literal: —and nothing more.
translations.idiomatic: There was nothing else in the message.

sentences.zh: 真卿得書大喜，因奏署大理評事、河北采訪支使。

translations.literal: Zhenqing was greatly pleased on receiving the letter and memorialized to appoint him Evaluator of the Court of Judicial Review and staff officer of the Hebei regional inspection.
translations.idiomatic: Delighted by the letter, Zhenqing memorialized the court to appoint Ning evaluator at the Court of Judicial Review and staff officer for the Hebei inspection circuit.

sentences.zh: 寧以長子屬母弟曰：「惟爾所適，茍不乏嗣，吾無累矣。」

translations.literal: Ning entrusted his eldest son to his younger brother by the same mother, saying, "Do as you see fit; so long as the line is not cut off, I shall have no further burdens."
translations.idiomatic: Ning placed his eldest son in his uterine younger brother's care, saying, "Raise him as you think best; if our line is not extinguished, I have nothing left to bind me.

sentences.zh: 因往平原，謂真卿曰：「先人有嗣矣！

translations.literal: He then went to Pingyuan and told Zhenqing, "Our forebears have heirs now!
translations.idiomatic: He went on to Pingyuan and told Zhenqing, "My ancestors have heirs again!

sentences.zh: 古所謂死有輕於鴻毛者，寧是也。

translations.literal: What the ancients called a death lighter than a goose feather—such is Ning's case.
translations.idiomatic: This is what the ancients meant when they said that some deaths weigh less than a goose feather.

sentences.zh: 願佐公以定危難。」

translations.literal: I wish to assist you, sir, in settling this peril."
translations.idiomatic: I wish to stand by you and help end this crisis."

sentences.zh: 真卿深然之。

translations.literal: Zhenqing deeply approved.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenqing was deeply moved and agreed wholeheartedly.

sentences.zh: 其後，寧計或不行，真卿迫蹙，棄郡，夜渡河而南，見肅宗於鳳翔。

translations.literal: Thereafter, when Ning's plans were sometimes not followed, Zhenqing was pressed hard, abandoned the commandery, crossed the river by night heading south, and met Emperor Suzong at Fengxiang.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Ning's counsel was not always heeded, Zhenqing found himself hard pressed, gave up the commandery, crossed the river by night to the south, and presented himself to Emperor Suzong at Fengxiang.

sentences.zh: 帝問拒賊之狀，真卿曰：「臣不用穆寧之言，功業不成。」

translations.literal: The emperor asked about resisting the rebels; Zhenqing said, "Had your servant not followed Mu Ning's counsel, my achievements would not have been accomplished."
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor asked how he had resisted the rebels, Zhenqing said, "Had I not taken Mu Ning's advice, I would have accomplished nothing.

sentences.zh: 帝奇之，發驛召寧，將以右職待之。

translations.literal: The emperor marveled at this, dispatched post-horses to summon Ning, and intended to treat him with a high office on the right.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was impressed and sent couriers by relay post to summon Ning, intending to reward him with a senior post.

sentences.zh: 會真卿以抗直失旨，事遂止。

translations.literal: But because Zhenqing had lost favor through his blunt uprightness, the matter came to nothing.
translations.idiomatic: But Zhenqing had fallen from favor for his blunt honesty, and the appointment never went through.

sentences.zh: 上元二年，累官至殿中侍御史，佐鹽鐵轉運使。

translations.literal: In the second year of Shangyuan he rose through successive posts to Attending Censor within the Palace and assisted the salt-and-iron transport commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: By the second year of Shangyuan he had risen to palace attending censor and was assisting the salt and iron transport commissioner.

sentences.zh: 副元帥李光弼以餉運不繼，或惡寧者，誣譖於光弼，光弼揚言欲殺寧。

translations.literal: The deputy commander-in-chief Li Guangbi, because supplies were not arriving in succession, had some who hated Ning slander him to Guangbi; Guangbi openly declared he would kill Ning.
translations.idiomatic: Deputy commander Li Guangbi, frustrated that supplies were not getting through, was persuaded by Ning's enemies to believe false charges against him; Guangbi openly threatened to have Ning executed.

sentences.zh: 寧直抵徐州見光弼，喻以大義，不為撓折。

translations.literal: Ning went straight to Xuzhou to see Guangbi, expounded the greater principle to him, and was not bent from his course.
translations.idiomatic: Ning went directly to Xuzhou to confront Guangbi, argued the larger duty at stake, and would not be cowed.

sentences.zh: 光弼深重之，寧得行其職。

translations.literal: Guangbi came to esteem him deeply, and Ning was able to carry out his duties.
translations.idiomatic: Guangbi came to respect him deeply, and Ning was allowed to do his work.

sentences.zh: 寶應初，轉侍御史，為河南轉運租庸鹽鐵等副使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Baoying he was transferred to Attending Censor and made deputy commissioner for Henan transport of land tax, labor corvée, and salt and iron.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Baoying era he became attending censor and deputy commissioner for Henan transport of taxes, corvée, and salt and iron.

sentences.zh: 明年，遷戶部員外郎。

translations.literal: The following year he was promoted to Vice Director of the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he was promoted to vice director in the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 無幾，加兼御史中丞，為河南、江南轉運使。

translations.literal: Before long he was additionally made Vice Censor-in-Chief and appointed transport commissioner for Henan and Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was also made vice censor-in-chief and transport commissioner for Henan and Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 廣德初，加庫部郎中。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Guangde he was additionally made Director of the Treasury Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Guangde era he was also made director in the Treasury Bureau.

sentences.zh: 是時河運不通，漕挽由漢、沔自商山達京師。

translations.literal: At that time the Grand Canal was not open; grain transport was hauled via the Han and Mian rivers from Shangshan to reach the capital.
translations.idiomatic: The canal route was blocked at the time, so grain had to be hauled along the Han and Mian rivers from Shangshan to the capital.

sentences.zh: 選鎮夏口者，詔以寧為鄂州刺史、鄂嶽沔都團練使，及淮西鄂嶽租庸鹽鐵沿江轉運使，賜金紫。

translations.literal: When someone was to be chosen to garrison Xiakou, an edict appointed Ning Prefect of Ezhou, Commander-in-Chief of Training for E, Yue, and Mian, and transport commissioner along the river for Huai-Xi, E-Yue land tax, corvée, and salt and iron, granting gold and purple.
translations.idiomatic: When the court needed a commander at Xiakou, Ning was appointed prefect of Ezhou, regional training commissioner for E, Yue, and Mian, and riverine transport commissioner for Huai-Xi and E-Yue taxes and salt and iron, with the gold-and-purple insignia of high rank.

sentences.zh: 時淮西節度使李忠臣貪暴不奉法，設防戍以稅商賈，又縱兵士剽劫，行人殆絕。

translations.literal: At that time the Huai-Xi military governor Li Zhongchen was greedy and violent and did not obey the law; he set garrisons to tax merchants, and also let soldiers plunder, so that travelers nearly ceased altogether.
translations.idiomatic: The Huai-Xi governor Li Zhongchen was greedy, brutal, and lawless: he posted garrisons to levy taxes on merchants and allowed his troops to rob travelers until traffic on the roads all but stopped.

sentences.zh: 與寧夾淮為理，憚寧威名，寇盜輒止。

translations.literal: He and Ning governed on opposite banks of the Huai; fearing Ning's renown, bandits and robbers at once ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Governing on opposite banks of the Huai from Ning, he feared Ning's reputation, and banditry quickly died down.

sentences.zh: 沔州別駕薛彥偉坐事忤旨，寧仗之致死。

translations.literal: Xue Yanwei, Vice Prefect of Mianzhou, offended the throne in a case; Ning beat him with staves until he died.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Yanwei, vice prefect of Mianzhou, ran afoul of the court in a legal matter; Ning had him beaten to death with staves.

sentences.zh: 寧坐貶虔州司馬，重貶昭州平集尉。

translations.literal: Ning was demoted on this account to Military Adjutant of Qianzhou, then further demoted to Revenue Clerk of Pingji in Zhaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Ning was demoted to military adjutant of Qianzhou and then further reduced to a minor revenue post in Zhaozhou.

sentences.zh: 大歷四年，起授監察御史，領轉運留後事於淄青。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Dali he was recalled and appointed Investigating Censor, taking charge of transport rear-affairs at Ziqing.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Dali he was recalled as investigating censor to oversee transport affairs at Ziqing.

sentences.zh: 間一年，改檢校司封郎中、兼侍御史，領轉運留後事於江西。

translations.literal: After a year he was changed to Acting Director of the Bureau of Enfeoffments, concurrently Attending Censor, in charge of transport rear-affairs in Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he became acting director of the Bureau of Enfeoffments and concurrent attending censor, managing transport affairs in Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 明年，拜檢校秘書少監，兼和州刺史，理有善政。

translations.literal: The next year he was appointed Acting Vice Director of the Palace Library, concurrently Prefect of Hezhou; his governance showed good administration.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was made acting vice director of the Palace Library and concurrent prefect of Hezhou, where his administration won praise.

sentences.zh: 居無何，官罷。

translations.literal: Before long he was dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was removed from his post.

sentences.zh: 代寧者以天寶版籍校見戶，誣以逋亡多，坐貶泉州司戶。

translations.literal: His successor checked registered households against the Tianbao registers, falsely charged many absconded households, and Ning was demoted to Revenue Clerk of Quanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His successor compared the tax rolls with the Tianbao census, falsely claimed that many households had fled, and Ning was demoted to revenue clerk in Quanzhou.

sentences.zh: 寧子贊，守闕三年告冤。

translations.literal: Ning's son Zan waited at the palace gates three years to plead his father's wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Ning's son Zan kept vigil at the palace gates for three years to plead his father's innocence.

sentences.zh: 詔遣御史按覆，而人戶增倍，詔書召寧，除右諭德。

translations.literal: An edict sent censors to investigate and verify; the registered population had in fact doubled; an edict summoned Ning and appointed him Right Mentor.
translations.idiomatic: The throne sent censors to reinvestigate; the registered population had actually doubled. Ning was recalled by edict and appointed right mentor of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 寧強毅，不能事權貴。

translations.literal: Ning was forceful and resolute and could not serve the powerful.
translations.idiomatic: Ning was tough and unyielding and would not court the powerful.

sentences.zh: 執政者以為不附己，且憚其難制，故處之散位。

translations.literal: Those in power thought him not attached to themselves and also feared he was hard to control, so they placed him in honorary posts.
translations.idiomatic: The chief ministers saw that he would not attach himself to them and feared his ungovernable temper, so they kept him in honorific posts without real power.

sentences.zh: 寧默默不得誌，且曰：「時不我容，我不時殉，則非吾之進也，在於退乎！」

translations.literal: Ning silently could not realize his aims and said, "If the times will not accommodate me and I do not accommodate the times, then advance is not my path—is withdrawal the answer?"
translations.idiomatic: Ning brooded in silence, unable to fulfill his ambitions, and said, "If the age will not have me and I will not bend to the age, then pressing forward is not my way—is it time to withdraw?

sentences.zh: 辭病居家，請告幾十旬者數矣。

translations.literal: He pleaded illness and stayed home, requesting leave for periods of many tens of days several times.
translations.idiomatic: He pleaded illness and retired to his home, repeatedly asking leave for months at a time.

sentences.zh: 親友強之，復一朝請。

translations.literal: Relatives and friends urged him, and he again attended court one morning.
translations.idiomatic: Friends and kin pressed him, and he returned to court for one more audience.

sentences.zh: 上居奉天，寧詣行在，拜秘書少監。

translations.literal: When the emperor resided at Fengtian, Ning went to the mobile court and was appointed Vice Director of the Palace Library.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor was at Fengtian, Ning went to the mobile court and was made vice director of the Palace Library.

sentences.zh: 興元初，改右庶子。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xingyuan he was changed to Right Vice Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Xingyuan era he was made right vice guardian of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 德宗還京師，寧曰：「可以行吾誌矣。」

translations.literal: When Dezong returned to the capital, Ning said, "I can now carry out my resolve."
translations.idiomatic: When Dezong returned to Chang'an, Ning said, "I can at last live as I intend.

sentences.zh: 因移病，罷歸東都。

translations.literal: He then pleaded transferred illness, resigned, and returned to the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: He cited illness, resigned his post, and retired to the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 貞元六年，就拜秘書監致仕。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Zhenyuan he was directly appointed Director of the Palace Library and retired from office.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Zhenyuan he accepted appointment as director of the Palace Library and retired from active service.

sentences.zh: 寧好學，善教諸子，家道以嚴稱。

translations.literal: Ning loved learning, was skilled at instructing his sons, and his household was known for its strictness.
translations.idiomatic: Ning was devoted to learning, taught his sons well, and his household was famed for its discipline.

sentences.zh: 事寡姊以悌聞。

translations.literal: He served his widowed elder sister and was known for fraternal devotion.
translations.idiomatic: His care for his widowed elder sister won him a reputation for filial devotion.

sentences.zh: 通達體命，未嘗服藥。

translations.literal: He understood the body's fate and never took medicine.
translations.idiomatic: He understood the body's natural course and never took medicine.

sentences.zh: 每誡諸子曰：「吾聞君子之事親，養誌為大，直道而已。

translations.literal: He often admonished his sons, saying, "I have heard that when a gentleman serves his parents, nurturing their aims is paramount—nothing but the straight path.
translations.idiomatic: He often warned his sons, "A gentleman serves his parents best by honoring their aims, not by fawning—only the straight path will do.

sentences.zh: 慎無為諂，吾之誌也。」

translations.literal: Take care never to flatter—that is my aim.
translations.idiomatic: Never stoop to flattery—that is what I live by.

sentences.zh: 貞元十年十月卒，時年七十九。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the tenth year of Zhenyuan he died, aged seventy-nine.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the tenth month of the tenth year of Zhenyuan, at the age of seventy-nine.

sentences.zh: 四子：贊、質、員、賞。

translations.literal: He had four sons: Zan, Zhi, Yuan, and Shang.
translations.idiomatic: He had four sons: Zan, Zhi, Yuan, and Shang.

sentences.zh: 寧子 贊贊，字相明，釋褐為濟源主簿。

translations.literal: Ning's son—Zan. Zan, styled Xiangming, upon leaving the russet robe was made Chief Clerk of Jiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Ning's son Zan, styled Xiangming, took his first office as chief clerk of Jiyuan.

sentences.zh: 時父寧為和州刺史，以剛直不屈於廉使，遂被誣奏，貶泉州司戶參軍。

translations.literal: At that time his father Ning was Prefect of Hezhou; because he was upright and would not yield to the fiscal inspector, he was falsely memorialized against and demoted to Revenue Clerk of Quanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His father Ning was then prefect of Hezhou; because he refused to bow to the fiscal inspector, he was falsely accused and demoted to revenue clerk in Quanzhou.

sentences.zh: 贊奔赴闕庭，號泣上訴。

translations.literal: Zan rushed to the palace gates, weeping and crying out his appeal.
translations.idiomatic: Zan hurried to the capital, weeping at the palace gates as he pleaded his father's case.

sentences.zh: 詔御史覆問，寧方得雪。

translations.literal: An edict sent censors to reinvestigate, and only then was Ning cleared.
translations.idiomatic: Censors were sent to reinvestigate, and Ning's name was cleared.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「令子申父之冤，憲臣奉君之命，楚劍不沖於牛斗，秦臺自洗於塵埃。」

translations.literal: An edict said, "The worthy son pleaded his father's wrong; the law officer carried out the ruler's command—the Chu sword did not clash with the Ox and Dipper; the Qin terrace washed itself of dust."
translations.idiomatic: An edict declared, "A worthy son has righted his father's wrong; the law officer has done the ruler's bidding—the sword of Chu need not strike the Ox and Dipper, for the mirror-stand of Qin cleanses itself of dust.

sentences.zh: 由是知名。

translations.literal: From this he became renowned.
translations.idiomatic: From that time his name was known throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 累遷京兆兵曹參軍、殿中侍御史，轉侍御史，分司東都。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to Military Staff Officer of the Capital District, Attending Censor within the Palace, then Attending Censor, serving in the Eastern Capital branch.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through posts as military staff officer in the capital district, palace attending censor, and attending censor with duty in the Eastern Capital branch.

sentences.zh: 時陜州觀察使盧嶽妾裴氏，以有子，嶽妻分財不及，訴於官，贊鞫其事。

translations.literal: At that time Pei, concubine of Lu Yue, Regional Inspector of Shaanzhou, because she had a son, was not given a share of property by Yue's wife and sued in court; Zan tried the case.
translations.idiomatic: Pei, a concubine of Shaanzhou inspector Lu Yue, had borne a son but was denied her share of the estate by Yue's wife; she brought suit, and Zan heard the case.

sentences.zh: 御史中丞盧佋佐之，令深繩裴罪。

translations.literal: Vice Censor-in-Chief Lu Bian assisted him and ordered Pei's crime bound tightly.
translations.idiomatic: Vice censor-in-chief Lu Bian took Yue's side and pressed for the harshest penalty against Pei.

sentences.zh: 贊持平不許。

translations.literal: Zan held to fairness and would not consent.
translations.idiomatic: Zan held to impartial justice and refused.

sentences.zh: 宰臣竇參與佋善，參、佋俱持權，怒贊以小事不受指使，遂下贊獄。

translations.literal: Chief minister Dou Can was friendly with Bian; Can and Bian both held power; angered that Zan on a minor matter would not accept orders, they had Zan thrown into prison.
translations.idiomatic: Chief minister Dou Can was allied with Bian; both men held real power and, furious that Zan would not bend on so small a matter, had him thrown into prison.

sentences.zh: 侍御史杜倫希其意，誣贊受裴之金，鞭其使以成其獄，甚急。

translations.literal: Attending Censor Du Lun gratified their intent, falsely charged Zan with receiving gold from Pei, and flogged his messenger to complete the case—very urgently.
translations.idiomatic: Attending censor Du Lun did their bidding, falsely accused Zan of taking bribes from Pei, and beat his servants to force a confession, pressing the case relentlessly.

sentences.zh: 贊弟賞，馳詣闕，撾登聞鼓。

translations.literal: Zan's younger brother Shang raced to the palace gates and struck the Petition Drum.
translations.idiomatic: Zan's younger brother Shang raced to the capital and beat the Petition Drum at the palace gates.

sentences.zh: 詔三司使覆理無驗，出為郴州刺史。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the Three Offices to reinvestigate; nothing was verified, and he was sent out as Prefect of Chenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The Three Offices were ordered to reinvestigate; the charges could not be sustained, and Zan was sent out as prefect of Chenzhou.

sentences.zh: 參敗，征拜刑部郎中。

translations.literal: When Can fell, Zan was summoned and appointed Director of the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: After Can's downfall, Zan was recalled and appointed director in the Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 因次對，德宗嘉其才，擢為御史中丞。

translations.literal: On a subsequent audience he impressed Dezong with his talent, and was promoted to Vice Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: At a later audience Dezong was impressed by his ability and promoted him to vice censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 時裴延齡判度支，以奸巧承恩。

translations.literal: At that time Pei Yanling oversaw the Department of Public Works and won favor through crafty deceit.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Yanling then controlled the treasury and curried favor through cunning and deceit.

sentences.zh: 屬吏有贓犯，贊鞫理承伏。

translations.literal: A subordinate official had committed embezzlement; Zan tried the case and obtained confession.
translations.idiomatic: When a subordinate was caught in embezzlement, Zan tried the case and obtained a confession.

sentences.zh: 延齡請曲法出之，贊三執不許，以款狀聞。

translations.literal: Yanling asked to bend the law and release him; Zan three times held firm and would not consent, reporting the confession to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Yanling asked that the law be bent to release the man; three times Zan refused and reported the full confession to the throne.

sentences.zh: 延齡誣贊不平，貶饒州別駕。

translations.literal: Yanling slandered Zan as biased and had him demoted to Vice Prefect of Raozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yanling accused Zan of partiality and had him demoted to vice prefect of Raozhou.

sentences.zh: 丁母憂，再轉虔、常二州刺史。

translations.literal: On mourning for his mother he was transferred in succession to Prefect of Qianzhou and Changzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After his mother's death he served in turn as prefect of Qianzhou and Changzhou.

sentences.zh: 憲宗即位，拜宣州刺史、御史中丞，充宣歙觀察使，所蒞皆有政聲。

translations.literal: When Xianzong took the throne, Zan was appointed Prefect of Xuanzhou and Vice Censor-in-Chief, filling the post of Regional Inspector of Xuan and She; wherever he governed there was praise for his administration.
translations.idiomatic: When Xianzong came to the throne, Zan was made prefect of Xuanzhou and vice censor-in-chief, with charge as regional inspector of Xuan and She; everywhere he served won a reputation for good government.

sentences.zh: 永貞元年十一月卒，時年五十八，贈工部尚書。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the first year of Yongzhen he died, aged fifty-eight; posthumously made Minister of Public Works.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the eleventh month of the first year of Yongzhen, at fifty-eight; the court posthumously appointed him minister of public works.

sentences.zh: 贊與弟質、員、賞以家行人材為搢紳所仰。

translations.literal: Zan and his brothers Zhi, Yuan, and Shang were admired by the gentry for their household conduct and personal talent.
translations.idiomatic: Zan and his brothers Zhi, Yuan, and Shang were admired throughout official society for their family discipline and personal gifts.

sentences.zh: 贊官達，父母尚無恙，家法清嚴。

translations.literal: When Zan had risen in office, his parents were still in good health, and the household rules were pure and strict.
translations.idiomatic: Even after Zan had risen high in office, while his parents were still alive the household remained governed by strict and austere rules.

sentences.zh: 贊兄弟奉指使，笞責如僮仆，贊最孝謹。

translations.literal: Zan and his brothers obeyed orders and accepted beatings like servants; Zan was most filial and careful.
translations.idiomatic: The brothers obeyed every parental command and accepted beatings like household servants; Zan was the most dutiful and deferential of them all.

sentences.zh: 寧子 質質強直，應制策入第三等。

translations.literal: Ning's son—Zhi. Zhi was forceful and upright; in the imperial examination policy essay he entered the third grade.
translations.idiomatic: Ning's son Zhi was forceful and upright and placed in the third rank on the imperial policy examination.

sentences.zh: 其所條對，至今傳之。

translations.literal: His itemized responses are transmitted to this day.
translations.idiomatic: His examination answers are still read today.

sentences.zh: 自補闕至給事中，時政得失，未嘗不先論諫。

translations.literal: From Remonstrance Officer to Supervising Secretary, on the gains and losses of current policy he never failed to speak first in remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: From remonstrance officer to supervising secretary, he was always the first to speak out on the rights and wrongs of current policy.

sentences.zh: 元和初，掌賦使院多擅禁系戶人，而有笞掠至死者。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yuanhe the Fiscal Commission often on its own authority imprisoned registered households, and there were cases of beating and flogging until death.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Yuanhe era the fiscal commission often imprisoned taxpayers on its own authority, and some died under the lash.

sentences.zh: 質乃論奏鹽鐵轉運司應決私鹽，系囚須與州府長吏監決。

translations.literal: Zhi then memorialized that when the Salt and Iron Transport Office should decide cases of private salt, imprisoned persons must be judged with the supervising presence of prefectural and district chief officials.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi memorialized that whenever the salt and iron transport office tried cases of illicit salt, local prefectural officials must be present to oversee any punishment of prisoners.

sentences.zh: 自是刑名畫一。

translations.literal: From this penalties and names were unified.
translations.idiomatic: From then on criminal procedure was standardized throughout the empire.

sentences.zh: 憲宗以王承宗叛，用內官吐突承璀為招討使。

translations.literal: Because Xianzong faced Wang Chengzong's rebellion, he used the inner eunuch Tutu Chengcui as Pacification Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Chengzong rebelled, Xianzong appointed the palace eunuch Tutu Chengcui pacification commissioner.

sentences.zh: 質率同列伏閣論奏，言自古無以中官為將帥者。

translations.literal: Zhi led his colleagues in prostrating themselves at the gate to remonstrate, saying that from antiquity there had never been inner eunuchs as generals and commanders.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi led his colleagues in a gate protest, arguing that never in history had eunuchs been made field commanders.

sentences.zh: 上雖改其名，心頗不悅，尋改質為太子左庶子。

translations.literal: Although the emperor changed Chengcui's title, he was quite displeased at heart and soon changed Zhi to Left Vice Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor changed Chengcui's title but was deeply displeased and soon transferred Zhi to left vice guardian of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 五年，坐與楊憑善，出為開州刺史。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, because he was friendly with Yang Ping, he was sent out as Prefect of Kaizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year, because of his association with Yang Ping, he was sent out as prefect of Kaizhou.

sentences.zh: 未幾卒。

translations.literal: Before long he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died not long afterward.

sentences.zh: 寧子 員員工文辭，尚節義。

translations.literal: Ning's son—Yuan. Yuan was skilled in literary composition and esteemed integrity and righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Ning's son Yuan was gifted in letters and held integrity and moral resolve above all else.

sentences.zh: 杜亞為東都留守，辟為從事、檢校員外郎。

translations.literal: When Du Ya was Protector-General of the Eastern Capital, he recruited him as staff officer and Acting Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: When Du Ya served as protector-general of the Eastern Capital, he summoned Yuan as a staff officer and acting vice director.

sentences.zh: 早卒，有文集十卷。

translations.literal: He died early and left a collected works in ten scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: He died young, leaving collected writings in ten scrolls.

sentences.zh: 質兄弟俱有令譽而和粹，世以「滋味」目之：贊俗而有格，為酪；

translations.literal: Zhi and his brothers all had fine reputations and were harmonious and pure; the age called them "flavors": Zan, popular yet with style, was cheese;
translations.idiomatic: Zhi and his brothers all enjoyed fine reputations and a gentle, harmonious character; contemporaries dubbed them "flavors": Zan, worldly yet principled, was cheese;

sentences.zh: 質美而多入，為酥；

translations.literal: Zhi was fine in quality and widely admired, was butter;
translations.idiomatic: Zhi, fine in character and widely admired, was butter;

sentences.zh: 員為醍醐；

translations.literal: Yuan was clarified butter;
translations.idiomatic: Yuan was the finest clarified butter;

sentences.zh: 賞為乳腐。

translations.literal: Shang was fermented curd.
translations.idiomatic: Shang was cottage curd.

sentences.zh: 近代士大夫言家法者，以穆氏為高。

translations.literal: Among recent scholar-officials who speak of family discipline, the Mu clan is held highest.
translations.idiomatic: Among recent scholar-officials who spoke of household discipline, the Mu clan was held in highest esteem.

sentences.zh: 崔邠崔邠，字處仁，清河武城人。

translations.literal: Cui Bin—Cui Bin, styled Churen, was a native of Wucheng in Qinghe.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Bin, styled Churen, was a native of Wucheng in Qinghe.

sentences.zh: 祖結，父倕，官卑。

translations.literal: His grandfather was Jie; his father Chui; both held low offices.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Jie and his father Chui both held only minor posts.

sentences.zh: 邠少舉進士，又登賢良方正科。

translations.literal: Bin passed the jinshi examination in youth and also passed the Xianliang Fangzheng examination.
translations.idiomatic: As a young man Bin passed the jinshi examination and also the Xianliang Fangzheng examination.

sentences.zh: 貞元中授渭南尉。

translations.literal: During the Zhenyuan era he was appointed District Commander of Weinan.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhenyuan era he was posted as district commander of Weinan.

sentences.zh: 遷拾遺、補闕。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Remonstrance Officer and Omission Officer.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to remonstrance officer and omission officer.

sentences.zh: 常疏論裴延齡，為時所知。

translations.literal: He often submitted memorials criticizing Pei Yanling and was known to the age.
translations.idiomatic: He often submitted memorials denouncing Pei Yanling and won renown in his day.

sentences.zh: 以兵部員外郎知制誥至中書舍人，凡七年。

translations.literal: From Vice Director of the Ministry of War with charge of edicts to Secretariat Drafter, altogether seven years.
translations.idiomatic: From vice director of the Ministry of War with charge of edicts to secretariat drafter, he served seven years in all.

sentences.zh: 又權知吏部選事。

translations.literal: He also acted as temporary director of the Ministry of Personnel's selections.
translations.idiomatic: He also served temporarily as director of personnel selections.

sentences.zh: 明年，為禮部侍郎，轉吏部侍郎，賜以金紫。

translations.literal: The next year he became Vice Minister of Rites, transferred to Vice Minister of Personnel, and was granted the gold seal and purple robe.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he became vice minister of rites, then vice minister of personnel, and was granted the gold seal and purple robe.

sentences.zh: 邠溫裕沈密，尤敦清儉。

translations.literal: Bin was warm and generous, deep and discreet, and especially devoted to purity and frugality.
translations.idiomatic: Bin was warm, generous, and reserved, and above all he practiced purity and frugality.

sentences.zh: 上亦器重之。

translations.literal: The emperor also valued him highly.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor held him in high regard as well.

sentences.zh: 裴垍將引為相，病難於承答，事竟寢。

translations.literal: Pei Ji was about to recommend him as chancellor, but illness made it hard for him to accept the appointment, and the matter ultimately fell through.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Ji was about to recommend him for the chancellorship, but illness made it difficult for him to accept, and the appointment never came to pass.

sentences.zh: 兄弟同時奉朝請者四人，頗以孝敬怡睦聞。

translations.literal: Four brothers at the same time attended court audiences and were widely known for filial piety, respect, and harmonious affection.
translations.idiomatic: Four brothers served at court at the same time and were widely known for filial devotion, mutual respect, and harmony.

sentences.zh: 後改太常卿，知吏部尚書銓事。

translations.literal: Later he was changed to Minister of Ceremonies with charge of the Ministry of Personnel's selection affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was later made minister of ceremonies and given charge of personnel selections.

sentences.zh: 故事，太常卿初上，大閱《四部樂》於署，觀者縱焉。

translations.literal: By precedent, when a new Minister of Ceremonies first assumed office, a grand review of the Four Sections of Music was held at the ministry, and spectators were unrestrained.
translations.idiomatic: By custom, when a new minister of ceremonies first took office, the ministry held a grand review of the Four Sections of Music, and onlookers were allowed to roam freely.

sentences.zh: 邠自私第去帽，親導母輿，公卿逢者回騎避之，衢路以為榮。

translations.literal: Bin removed his hat at his private residence, personally guided his mother's carriage, and when high officials encountered them they turned their horses aside; the thoroughfare took it as an honor.
translations.idiomatic: Leaving his private residence, Bin removed his hat and personally guided his mother's carriage; high officials who met them turned aside, and the whole street regarded it as an honor.

sentences.zh: 居母憂，歲余卒，元和十年三月也，時年六十二。

translations.literal: While in mourning for his mother, he died after more than a year, in the third month of Yuanhe 10, at the age of sixty-two.
translations.idiomatic: While mourning his mother, he died a little over a year later, in the third month of Yuanhe 10, at the age of sixty-two.

sentences.zh: 贈吏部尚書，謚曰文簡。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted Minister of Personnel, with the posthumous title Cultured and Simple.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made minister of personnel and given the posthumous title Cultured and Simple.

sentences.zh: 邠弟 鄯弟鄯、郾、鄲等六人。

translations.literal: Bin's brothers: Shan, Yan, Tan, and six in all.
translations.idiomatic: Bin's brothers included Shan, Yan, and Tan—six brothers in all.

sentences.zh: 子璀、璜，璀子彥融，皆登進士第，歷位臺閣。

translations.literal: His sons Cui and Huang; Cui's son Yanrong—all passed the jinshi examination and served in the central secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: His sons Cui and Huang, and Cui's son Yanrong, all passed the jinshi examination and rose to posts in the central secretariat.

sentences.zh: 鄯少有文學，舉進士。

translations.literal: Shan had literary talent from youth and passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: Shan showed literary promise from youth and passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 元和中，歷監察御史。

translations.literal: During the Yuanhe era he served as Investigating Censor.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yuanhe era he served as investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 太和元年十月，自太子詹事拜左金吾衛大將軍。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the first year of Tahe, he was promoted from Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent to General of the Left Golden Crown Guard.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of Tahe 1 he was promoted from grand mentor of the heir apparent to general of the Left Golden Crown Guard.

sentences.zh: 鄯昆弟六人，仕官皆至三品。

translations.literal: Shan's six brothers all reached third rank in office.
translations.idiomatic: All six of Shan's brothers rose to third rank.

sentences.zh: 邠、郾、鄲三人，知貢舉，掌銓衡。

translations.literal: Bin, Yan, and Tan—the three of them directed the imperial examinations and managed personnel selections.
translations.idiomatic: Bin, Yan, and Tan all directed the imperial examinations and oversaw personnel appointments.

sentences.zh: 冠族聞望，為時名德。

translations.literal: A foremost clan in reputation and prestige, they were celebrated men of virtue in their age.
translations.idiomatic: A leading clan in prestige and renown, they were celebrated as men of virtue in their time.

sentences.zh: 鄯太和九年冬，為左金吾大將軍，無病暴亡。

translations.literal: In the winter of the ninth year of Tahe, while serving as General of the Left Golden Crown Guard, Shan died suddenly without illness.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of Tahe 9, while serving as general of the Left Golden Crown Guard, Shan died suddenly though he had shown no sign of illness.

sentences.zh: 不旬日有訓、註之亂，其亂始自金吾。

translations.literal: Within ten days came the rebellion of Xun and Zhu, and the disorder began with the Golden Crown Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Within ten days the rebellion of Xun and Zhu broke out, and the uprising began in the Golden Crown Guard.

sentences.zh: 君子乃知鄯之亡，崔氏積善之征也。

translations.literal: Men of virtue then understood that Shan's death was a sign of the Cui clan's accumulated goodness.
translations.idiomatic: Men of discernment then understood that Shan's death was Heaven's reward for the Cui clan's accumulated virtue.

sentences.zh: 贈禮部尚書。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made minister of rites.

sentences.zh: 子瑄。

translations.literal: His son was Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Xuan.

sentences.zh: 邠弟 郾郾，字廣略，舉進士，平判入等，授集賢殿校書郎。

translations.literal: Bin's brother—Yan. Yan, styled Guanglue, passed the jinshi examination, entered the pingpan examination with distinction, and was appointed Collator of the Hall of Assembled Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: Bin's brother Yan, styled Guanglue, passed the jinshi examination, distinguished himself on the pingpan examination, and was appointed collator in the Hall of Assembled Worthies.

sentences.zh: 三命升朝，為監察御史、刑部員外郎。

translations.literal: Three times summoned to court, he served as Investigating Censor and Vice Director of the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: Summoned to court three times, he served as investigating censor and vice director of the Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 資質秀偉，神情重雅，人望而愛之，終不可舍，不知者以為事高簡，拘靜默耳。

translations.literal: His endowment was elegant and imposing, his bearing grave and refined; people who saw him loved him and could not bear to part from him. Those who did not know him thought him merely aloof, austere, and overly silent.
translations.idiomatic: Handsome and imposing in bearing, grave and refined in manner, he drew people's affection at first sight and they hated to leave his company; those who did not know him took him for merely proud, austere, and taciturn.

sentences.zh: 居內憂，釋服為吏部員外。

translations.literal: While in mourning for a parent, after the mourning period ended he became Vice Director of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: After completing mourning for a parent, he returned to office as vice director of the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 奸吏不敢欺，孤寒無援者未嘗留滯，銓敘之美，為時所稱。

translations.literal: Corrupt clerks did not dare deceive him; the isolated and poor without patrons were never delayed; the excellence of his personnel assignments was praised by the age.
translations.idiomatic: Corrupt clerks did not dare cheat him, and poor men without patrons were never left waiting; the fairness of his appointments won wide praise.

sentences.zh: 再遷左司郎中。

translations.literal: He was promoted again to Director of the Left Department.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted again to director of the left department.

sentences.zh: 元和十三年，鄭余慶為禮儀詳定使，選時有禮學者共事，以郾為詳定判官、吏部郎中。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Yuanhe, Zheng Yuqing served as Commissioner for Ceremonial Review and selected scholars of ritual to assist him; Yan was appointed review adjudicator and Director of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanhe 13, when Zheng Yuqing served as commissioner for ceremonial review and chose ritual scholars to assist him, Yan was made review adjudicator and director of the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 十五年，遷諫議大夫。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he was promoted to Remonstrance Grandee.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year he was promoted to remonstrance grandee.

sentences.zh: 穆宗即位，荒於禽酒，坐朝常晚。

translations.literal: When Muzong took the throne, he indulged in hunting and wine and often held court late.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Muzong came to the throne, he abandoned himself to hunting and wine and often held court late.

sentences.zh: 郾與同列鄭覃等延英切諫。

translations.literal: Yan, together with his colleague Zheng Tan and others, remonstrated earnestly in the Yenying Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Yan and his colleagues Zheng Tan and others remonstrated with him earnestly in the Yenying Hall.

sentences.zh: 穆宗甚嘉之，畋遊稍簡。

translations.literal: Muzong greatly praised them, and his hunting excursions were slightly reduced.
translations.idiomatic: Muzong greatly commended them, and his hunting outings grew somewhat less frequent.

sentences.zh: 長慶中，轉給事中。

translations.literal: During the Changqing era he was transferred to Supervising Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: During the Changqing era he was made supervising secretary.

sentences.zh: 昭湣即位，選侍講學士，轉中書舍人。

translations.literal: When Zhaomin took the throne, Yan was selected as Lecturing Academician and transferred to Secretariat Drafter.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhaomin came to the throne, Yan was chosen as lecturing academician and promoted to secretariat drafter.

sentences.zh: 入思政殿謝恩，奏曰：「陛下用臣為侍講，半歲有余，未嘗問臣經義。

translations.literal: Entering the Hall of Zheng'en to thank the throne for his favor, he memorialized: "Your Majesty appointed me as lecturer more than half a year ago, yet you have never asked me about the meaning of the classics.
translations.idiomatic: Entering the Hall of Zheng'en to thank the throne, he said, "Your Majesty made me your lecturer more than half a year ago, yet you have never asked me about the classics.

sentences.zh: 今蒙轉改，實慚屍素，有愧厚恩。」

translations.literal: Now, receiving this transfer and promotion, I am truly ashamed to hold office without performing my duties and feel guilty before your generous favor."
translations.idiomatic: Now that I have been promoted again, I am ashamed to occupy my post without earning it, and I feel unworthy of your great kindness."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「朕機務稍閑，即當請益。」

translations.literal: The emperor said, "When my routine state affairs grow somewhat less pressing, I shall seek your instruction."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied, "When my daily duties grow a little less pressing, I shall ask you to instruct me."

sentences.zh: 高鉞曰：「陛下意雖樂善，既未延接儒生，天下之人，寧知重道？」

translations.literal: Gao Kui said, "Though Your Majesty's intent delights in goodness, since you have not yet received Confucian scholars, how can people under heaven know to esteem the Way?"
translations.idiomatic: Gao Kui said, "Your Majesty's heart may delight in virtue, but if you do not yet receive Confucian scholars, how can the people know that the Way is honored?"

sentences.zh: 帝深引咎，賜之錦彩。

translations.literal: The emperor deeply took blame upon himself and granted them brocade and silk.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor took the rebuke deeply to heart and rewarded them with brocade and silk.

sentences.zh: 郾退，與同列高重抄撮《六經》嘉言要道，區分事類，凡十卷，名曰《諸經纂要》，冀人主易於省覽。

translations.literal: Yan withdrew and, with his colleague Gao Chong, excerpted fine words and essential points from the Six Classics, divided them by category into ten scrolls, and titled the work Collected Essentials of the Classics, hoping the ruler could review them easily.
translations.idiomatic: Yan then withdrew and, with his colleague Gao Chong, compiled the finest passages and essential teachings of the Six Classics, arranged them by topic in ten scrolls under the title Collected Essentials of the Classics, and hoped the ruler might review them with ease.

sentences.zh: 上嘉之，賜錦彩二百匹、銀器等。

translations.literal: The emperor praised it and granted two hundred bolts of brocade, silver vessels, and other gifts.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor commended the work and granted two hundred bolts of brocade, silver vessels, and other gifts.

sentences.zh: 其年轉禮部侍郎，東都試舉人。

translations.literal: That year he was transferred to Vice Minister of Rites and tested candidates in the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: That same year he became vice minister of rites and examined candidates in the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 凡兩歲掌貢士，平心閱試，賞拔藝能，所擢者無非名士，至大中、咸通之代，為輔相名卿者十數人。

translations.literal: For two years he directed the presenting of scholars, reviewed the examinations with an impartial heart, and rewarded talent; those he advanced were all famed scholars, and by the Dazhong and Xiantong eras more than ten had become chancellors and eminent ministers.
translations.idiomatic: For two years he oversaw the examinations, judged them impartially, and promoted men of real ability; every candidate he chose was a noted scholar, and by the Dazhong and Xiantong eras more than ten of them had become chancellors and leading ministers.

sentences.zh: 出為陜州觀察使。

translations.literal: He was sent out as Regional Inspector of Shaanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as regional inspector of Shaanzhou.

sentences.zh: 舊弊有上供不足，奪吏俸以益之，歲八十萬，郾以廉使常用之直代之。

translations.literal: An old abuse held that when tribute payments fell short, clerks' salaries were seized to make up the deficit—eighty thousand per year; Yan used the fiscal inspector's regular expenses to cover it instead.
translations.idiomatic: An old abuse had been to make up shortfalls in tribute payments by seizing clerks' salaries—eighty thousand cash a year; Yan covered the deficit out of the fiscal inspector's regular operating funds instead.

sentences.zh: 居二年，政績聞於朝。

translations.literal: After two years his achievements were known at court.
translations.idiomatic: After two years his record of governance was known at court.

sentences.zh: 遷鄂嶽安黃等州觀察使。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Regional Inspector of E, Yue, An, Huang, and other prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to regional inspector of E, Yue, An, Huang, and neighboring prefectures.

sentences.zh: 又五年，移浙西道都團練觀察使，至，用寬政安疲人。

translations.literal: Five years later he was moved to Defense Commissioner and Regional Inspector of the Zhexi Circuit; upon arrival he used lenient governance to settle the weary populace.
translations.idiomatic: Five years later he was moved to defense commissioner and regional inspector of Zhexi; on taking up his post he governed leniently and brought rest to a worn-out people.

sentences.zh: 及居鄂渚，則峻法嚴刑，未常貰一死罪。

translations.literal: When he was at Ezhou, by contrast he applied stern laws and severe punishments and never once pardoned a capital offense.
translations.idiomatic: At Ezhou, by contrast, he enforced harsh laws and severe punishments and never once pardoned a capital crime.

sentences.zh: 江湖之間，萑蒲是叢，因造蒙沖小艦，上下千里，期月而盡獲群盜。

translations.literal: Between the rivers and lakes bandits clustered thick as reeds; he therefore built light assault boats and, up and down a thousand li, within a month captured all the bandit bands.
translations.idiomatic: Bandits infested the rivers and lakes like weeds in a marsh; he built light assault boats, swept a thousand li of waterways, and within a month had captured every bandit band.

sentences.zh: 凡三按廉車，率由清簡少事，財用有余，遂寧泰。

translations.literal: In all three tours as integrity commissioner he generally governed through purity and simplicity with few affairs; funds had surplus, and peace was achieved.
translations.idiomatic: In three tours as integrity commissioner he governed with clean, simple administration and little fuss; revenues exceeded expenses, and the region grew tranquil.

sentences.zh: 開成元年卒，年六十九，贈吏部尚書，謚曰德。

translations.literal: He died in the first year of Kaicheng at the age of sixty-nine, was posthumously granted Minister of Personnel, and was given the posthumous title Virtue.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Kaicheng 1 at the age of sixty-nine, was posthumously made minister of personnel, and was given the posthumous title Virtue.

sentences.zh: 郾與兄邠、弟鄲等皆有令譽。

translations.literal: Yan, his elder brother Bin, his younger brother Tan, and the others all had fine reputations.
translations.idiomatic: Yan, his elder brother Bin, his younger brother Tan, and the rest all enjoyed fine reputations.

sentences.zh: 而郾疏財恢廓，昆仲所不及。

translations.literal: But Yan was free with wealth and magnanimous, which his brothers could not match.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Yan alone was open-handed and magnanimous with wealth, a quality his brothers could not equal.

sentences.zh: 子瑤、瑰、瑾、珮、璆。

translations.literal: His sons were Yao, Gui, Jin, Pei, and Qiu.
translations.idiomatic: His sons were Yao, Gui, Jin, Pei, and Qiu.

sentences.zh: 郾子 瑤瑤，太和三年登進士第，出佐籓方，入升朝列，累至中書舍人。

translations.literal: Yan's son—Yao. Yao passed the jinshi examination in the third year of Tahe, went out to assist a regional command, entered the court ranks, and rose in succession to Secretariat Drafter.
translations.idiomatic: Yan's son Yao passed the jinshi examination in Tahe 3, served in regional staff posts, entered court service, and rose to secretariat drafter.

sentences.zh: 大中六年，知貢舉，旋拜禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Dazhong he directed the imperial examinations and was soon appointed Vice Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: In Dazhong 6 he directed the imperial examinations and was soon made vice minister of rites.

sentences.zh: 出為浙西觀察使，又遷鄂州刺史、鄂嶽觀察使，終於位。

translations.literal: He was sent out as Regional Inspector of Zhexi, then transferred to Prefect of Ezhou and Regional Inspector of E and Yue, and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as regional inspector of Zhexi, later became prefect of Ezhou and regional inspector of E and Yue, and died in office.

sentences.zh: 瑰、珮、璆官至郎署給諫。

translations.literal: Gui, Pei, and Qiu reached posts in the ministries and remonstrance offices.
translations.idiomatic: Gui, Pei, and Qiu rose to posts in the ministries and remonstrance offices.

sentences.zh: 郾子 謹謹，大中十年登進士第，累居使府，歷尚書郎、知制誥。

translations.literal: Yan's son—Jin. Jin passed the jinshi examination in the tenth year of Dazhong, repeatedly served in commissioner offices, and passed through ministry director posts with charge of edicts.
translations.idiomatic: Yan's son Jin passed the jinshi examination in Dazhong 10, served repeatedly in commissioner offices, and rose through ministry director posts to charge of edicts.

sentences.zh: 咸通十三年，知貢舉，選拔頗為得人。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Xiantong he directed the imperial examinations, and his selections were quite well chosen.
translations.idiomatic: In Xiantong 13 he directed the imperial examinations and chose his candidates with notable success.

sentences.zh: 尋拜禮部侍郎，出為湖南觀察使。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was appointed Vice Minister of Rites and sent out as Regional Inspector of Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made vice minister of rites and sent out as regional inspector of Hunan.

sentences.zh: 邠弟 鄲鄲，登進士第，累遷監察御史，三遷考功郎中。

translations.literal: Bin's brother—Tan. Tan passed the jinshi examination, was repeatedly promoted to Investigating Censor, and was promoted three times to Director of Merit Evaluation.
translations.idiomatic: Bin's brother Tan passed the jinshi examination, rose to investigating censor, and was promoted three times to director of merit evaluation.

sentences.zh: 太和三年，以本官充翰林學士，轉中書舍人。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tahe, while retaining his existing post he was appointed Hanlin Academician and transferred to Secretariat Drafter.
translations.idiomatic: In Tahe 3 he was made Hanlin academician while retaining his existing post and was promoted to secretariat drafter.

sentences.zh: 六年，罷學士。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was dismissed from the academician post.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was removed from the Hanlin academy.

sentences.zh: 八年，為工部侍郎、集賢殿學士，權知禮部，真拜兵部侍郎，本官判吏部東銓事。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he became Vice Minister of Works and Academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies, acted as temporary director of the Ministry of Rites, was formally appointed Vice Minister of War, and with his existing post adjudicated the Eastern Branch selections of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he became vice minister of works and academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies, served temporarily as director of the Ministry of Rites, was formally appointed vice minister of war, and continued to oversee the eastern branch of personnel selections.

sentences.zh: 文宗勤於政道，每苦選曹訛弊，延英謂宰臣曰：「吏部殊不選才，安得摭實無濫，可厘革否？」

translations.literal: Wenzong was diligent in governance and often troubled by corruption in the selection bureau; in the Yenying Hall he said to the chief ministers, "The Ministry of Personnel scarcely selects talent—how can we gather truth without abuse? Can it be reformed?"
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wenzong was diligent in government and often vexed by corruption in the selection bureau; in the Yenying Hall he asked his chief ministers, "The Ministry of Personnel scarcely chooses men of talent—how can appointments be grounded in fact and kept free of abuse? Can this be reformed?"

sentences.zh: 李石對曰：「令錄可以商量，他官且宜循舊。」

translations.literal: Li Shi replied, "County magistrates and recorders can be discussed; other offices should for now follow precedent."
translations.idiomatic: Li Shi answered, "We might discuss county magistrates and recorders, but for other offices it would be best to follow precedent for now."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「循舊如配官耳，賢不肖安能甄別？」

translations.literal: The emperor said, "Following precedent is like assigning offices at random—how can the worthy and unworthy be distinguished?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Following precedent is no better than assigning offices by lot—how can the worthy and unworthy be told apart?"

sentences.zh: 帝召三銓謂之曰：「卿等比選令錄，如何註擬？」

translations.literal: The emperor summoned the three selection directors and said, "When you recently selected magistrates and recorders, how did you note your appointments?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor summoned the three selection directors and asked, "In your recent selection of magistrates and recorders, how did you decide their appointments?"

sentences.zh: 鄲對曰：「資敘相當，問其為治之術，視可否而擬之。」

translations.literal: Tan replied, "When qualifications and seniority matched, we asked their methods of governance and judged suitability before proposing appointments."
translations.idiomatic: Tan answered, "When seniority and qualifications matched the post, we asked about their methods of governance and proposed appointments according to what they could do."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「依資合得，而才劣者何授？」

translations.literal: The emperor said, "When by seniority one qualifies but talent is inferior, what post is given?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked, "When a man qualifies by seniority but lacks ability, what post do you give him?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「與邊遠慢官。」

translations.literal: He replied, "Remote frontier posts of low importance."
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "A remote frontier post of little consequence."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「如以不肖之才治邊民，則疾苦可知也。

translations.literal: The emperor said, "If unworthy talent governs frontier people, their suffering is predictable.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "If incapable men govern frontier people, their suffering is easy to imagine.

sentences.zh: 凡朝廷求理，遠近皆須得人。

translations.literal: Whenever the court seeks good governance, near and far all require the right men.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the court seeks good order, both near and far require the right men.

sentences.zh: 茍非其才，人受其弊矣。」

translations.literal: If it is not the right talent, the people suffer the harm."
translations.idiomatic: If the wrong man is chosen, the people bear the cost."

sentences.zh: 尋拜吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was appointed Vice Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed vice minister of personnel.

sentences.zh: 開成二年，出為宣州刺史，兼御史中丞、宣歙觀察使。

translations.literal: In the second year of Kaicheng he was sent out as Prefect of Xuanzhou, concurrently Vice Censor-in-Chief and Regional Inspector of Xuan and She.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaicheng 2 he was sent out as prefect of Xuanzhou, concurrently vice censor-in-chief and regional inspector of Xuan and She.

sentences.zh: 四年，入為太常卿。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he entered court as Minister of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he returned to court as minister of ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 七月，以本官同中書門下平章事，尋加中書侍郎、銀青光祿大夫。

translations.literal: In the seventh month, while retaining his existing post he was made Associate Director of the Chancellery and Grand Councilor, and soon afterward was given Vice Director of the Secretariat and the title Grand Master of Splendid Brightness with Silver Seal.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month he was made associate director of the chancellery and grand councilor while retaining his existing post, and soon afterward was also made vice director of the secretariat and grand master of splendid brightness with silver seal.

sentences.zh: 會昌初，李德裕用事，與鄲弟兄素善。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Huichang, when Li Deyu held power, he was on good terms with Tan and his brothers.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Huichang era, when Li Deyu held power, he had long been on good terms with Tan and his brothers.

sentences.zh: 鄲在相位累年，歷方鎮、太子師保卒。

translations.literal: Tan served in the chancellorship for many years, passed through regional commands and posts as tutor to the heir apparent, and then died.
translations.idiomatic: Tan remained in the chancellorship for many years, later served in regional commands and as tutor to the heir apparent, and died in those posts.

sentences.zh: 竇群竇群，字丹列，扶風平陵人。

translations.literal: Dou Qun—Dou Qun—style name Danlie, a native of Pingling in Fufeng.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Qun, styled Danlie, was a native of Pingling in Fufeng.

sentences.zh: 祖亶，同昌郡司馬。

translations.literal: His grandfather Dan was Military Assistant of Tongchang Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Dan had served as military assistant of Tongchang Commandery.

sentences.zh: 父叔向，以工詩稱，代宗朝，官至左拾遺。

translations.literal: His father Shuxiang was famed for skill in poetry; during the reign of Emperor Daizong he rose to Left Reminder.
translations.idiomatic: His father Shuxiang was known for his poetic mastery; under Emperor Daizong he rose to the post of Left Reminder of the Imperial Archives.

sentences.zh: 群兄常、牟，弟鞏，皆登進士第，唯群獨為處士，隱居毗陵，以節操聞。

translations.literal: Qun's elder brothers Chang and Mou and younger brother Gong all passed the jinshi examination; only Qun alone remained a retired scholar, living in seclusion at Piling, renowned for integrity and conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Qun's elder brothers Chang and Mou and his younger brother Gong all passed the jinshi examination, but Qun alone remained a private scholar in seclusion at Piling, where his integrity won wide renown.

sentences.zh: 及母卒，嚙一指置棺中，因廬墓次終喪。

translations.literal: When his mother died, he bit off one finger and placed it in the coffin, then built a hut by the tomb and completed the full mourning period there.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died, he bit off one of his fingers and placed it in her coffin, then built a mourning hut beside her tomb and lived there through the full mourning period.

sentences.zh: 後學《春秋》於啖助之門人盧庇者，著書三十四卷，號《史記名臣疏》。

translations.literal: Later he studied the Spring and Autumn Annals under Lu Pi, a disciple of Tan Zhu, and composed a work in thirty-four chapters entitled Exegesis on Eminent Ministers in the Records of the Grand Historian.
translations.idiomatic: He later studied the Spring and Autumn Annals under Lu Pi, a disciple of Tan Zhu, and produced a thirty-four-chapter work entitled Exegesis on Eminent Ministers in the Records of the Grand Historian.

sentences.zh: 貞元中，蘇州刺史韋夏卿以丘園茂異薦，兼獻其書，不報。

translations.literal: During the Zhenyuan era, Suzhou Prefect Wei Xiaqing recommended him as an eminent recluse of exceptional merit and also submitted his book, but there was no response.
translations.idiomatic: During Zhenyuan, Wei Xiaqing, prefect of Suzhou, recommended him as an exceptional hermit of outstanding character and submitted his book as well, but the court did not respond.

sentences.zh: 及夏卿入為吏部侍郎，改京兆尹，中謝日，因對復薦群。

translations.literal: When Xiaqing entered court as Vice Minister of the Ministry of Personnel and was transferred to be Metropolitan Governor of Jingzhao, on the day of his audience of thanks he took the occasion in a private audience to recommend Qun again.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiaqing was summoned to the capital as vice minister of personnel and transferred to metropolitan governor of Jingzhao, he used his audience of thanks to recommend Qun once more in a private memorial.

sentences.zh: 征拜左拾遺，遷侍御史，充入蕃使秘書監張薦判官。

translations.literal: Qun was summoned and appointed Left Reminder, promoted to Censor, and assigned as aide to Zhang Jian, Director of the Secretariat and envoy to the foreign lands.
translations.idiomatic: Qun was summoned and appointed Left Reminder, then promoted to censor and named aide to Zhang Jian, director of the Secretariat, who was then serving as envoy to the barbarian courts.

sentences.zh: 群因入對，奏曰：「陛下即位二十年，始自草澤擢臣為拾遺，是難其進也。

translations.literal: On being received in audience, Qun memorialized, saying, "Your Majesty has reigned twenty years before raising me from the wilds to the post of Reminder—this shows how hard it is to advance.
translations.idiomatic: When Qun was received in audience, he said, "Your Majesty has been on the throne twenty years before raising me from obscurity to the post of Reminder—surely advancement is difficult indeed.

sentences.zh: 今陛下以二十年難進之臣，用為和蕃判官，一何易也？」

translations.literal: Now Your Majesty uses a man who was hard to advance for twenty years as aide for pacifying the barbarians—how very easy that is!
translations.idiomatic: Yet now Your Majesty appoints a man who waited twenty years for office to serve as aide for a marriage mission to the barbarians—how very easy advancement has become!

sentences.zh: 德宗異其言，留之，復為侍御史。

translations.literal: Dezong was struck by his words, kept him, and restored him to the post of Censor.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Dezong was impressed by his boldness, kept him at court, and restored him to his post as censor.

sentences.zh: 王叔文之黨柳宗元、劉禹錫皆慢群，群不附之。

translations.literal: Liu Zongyuan and Liu Yuxi, members of Wang Shuwen's faction, all treated Qun with contempt; Qun would not attach himself to them.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zongyuan and Liu Yuxi, allies of Wang Shuwen, looked down on Qun, and Qun refused to join their faction.

sentences.zh: 其黨議欲貶群官，韋執誼止之。

translations.literal: The faction discussed demoting Qun, but Wei Zhiyi stopped it.
translations.idiomatic: His faction debated demoting Qun from office, but Wei Zhiyi dissuaded them.

sentences.zh: 群嘗謁王叔文，叔文命撤榻而進。

translations.literal: Qun once called on Wang Shuwen; Shuwen ordered the couch removed and had him come forward.
translations.idiomatic: When Qun once paid a call on Wang Shuwen, Shuwen had the receiving couch taken away and bade him step forward.

sentences.zh: 群揖之曰：「夫事有不可知者。」

translations.literal: Qun bowed and said, "There are matters one cannot foresee.
translations.idiomatic: Qun bowed and said, "There are turns of fortune no man can foresee.

sentences.zh: 叔文曰：「如何？」

translations.literal: Shuwen said, "How so?"
translations.idiomatic: Shuwen asked, "What do you mean?"

sentences.zh: 群曰：「去年李實伐恩恃貴，傾動一時，此時公逡巡路旁，乃江南一吏耳。

translations.literal: Qun said, "Last year Li Shi relied on favor and high rank, and shook the court for a time; at that time you were hesitating on the roadside—nothing but a lowly clerk from the south.
translations.idiomatic: Qun replied, "Last year Li Shi traded on imperial favor and shook the court for a season; at that time you were lingering on the margins—nothing but an obscure clerk from south of the Yangtze.

sentences.zh: 今公已處實形勢，又安得不慮路旁有公者乎？」

translations.literal: Now you occupy real power—how can you fail to consider that someone like you may be waiting on the roadside?"
translations.idiomatic: Now you hold real power—should you not fear that someone like you today may be waiting in the wings tomorrow?"

sentences.zh: 叔文雖異其言，竟不之用。

translations.literal: Although Shuwen was struck by his words, in the end he did not employ him.
translations.idiomatic: Shuwen was startled by the warning, but in the end he never made use of Qun.

sentences.zh: 憲宗即位，轉膳部員外，兼侍御史知雜，出為唐州刺史。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xianzong took the throne, Qun was transferred to Vice Director of the Ministry of Rites in the Bureau of Banquets, concurrently Censor in charge of miscellaneous matters, then sent out as Prefect of Tangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xianzong acceded, Qun was promoted to vice director in the banquet office of the Ministry of Rites and concurrent chief censor, then appointed prefect of Tangzhou.

sentences.zh: 節度使于頔素聞其名，既謁見，群危言激切，頔甚悅。

translations.literal: Military Commissioner Yu Di had long heard his reputation; when Qun paid his respects, he spoke stern and pointed words, and Di was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Military Commissioner Yu Di had long known Qun's reputation; at their first meeting Qun spoke with urgent frankness, and Di was deeply pleased.

sentences.zh: 奏留充山南東道節度副使、檢校兵部郎中，兼御史中丞，賜紫金魚袋。

translations.literal: Di memorialized to keep him as Deputy Military Commissioner of the Shannan East Circuit, Acting Chief of the Bureau of Military Affairs in the Ministry of War, concurrently Vice Censor-in-Chief, and granted him the purple robe and gold fish tally.
translations.idiomatic: Yu memorialized to retain him as deputy commissioner of the Shannan East Circuit, acting chief of the bureau of military affairs, and concurrent vice censor-in-chief, and granted him the purple robe and gold fish tally.

sentences.zh: 宰相武元衡、李吉甫皆愛重之，召入為吏部郎中。

translations.literal: Chief Ministers Wu Yuanheng and Li Jifu both valued him highly and summoned him to serve as Chief of the Bureau of Appointments in the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Chief ministers Wu Yuanheng and Li Jifu both admired him and recalled him to the capital as chief of the appointments bureau in the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 元衡輔政，舉群代己為中丞。

translations.literal: When Yuanheng served as chief minister, he recommended Qun to replace himself as Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: While serving as chief minister, Wu Yuanheng recommended Qun to succeed him as censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 群奏刑部郎中呂溫、羊士諤為御史。

translations.literal: Qun memorialized to appoint Lu Wen and Yang Shiyan, chiefs of the Bureau of Punishments, as censors.
translations.idiomatic: Qun recommended Lu Wen and Yang Shiyan of the Ministry of Justice for appointment as censors.

sentences.zh: 吉甫以羊、呂險躁，持之數日不下，群等怒怨吉甫。

translations.literal: Jifu regarded Yang and Lu as rash and dangerous, held the memorial for several days without issuing it, and Qun and the others grew angry and resentful toward Jifu.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jifu deemed Yang and Lu rash and unreliable, held their nominations for days without approval, and Qun and his allies came to resent him bitterly.

sentences.zh: 三年八月，吉甫罷相，出鎮淮南，群等欲因失恩傾之。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the third year, Jifu was removed from the chancellorship and sent out to command Huainan; Qun and his followers wished to use his loss of favor to bring him down.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the third year Jifu was dismissed from the chancellorship and posted to Huainan; Qun and his allies hoped to exploit his fall from favor to destroy him.

sentences.zh: 吉甫嘗召術士陳登宿於安邑里第。

translations.literal: Jifu had once summoned the adept Chen Deng to lodge at his mansion in Anyi Lane.
translations.idiomatic: Jifu had once summoned the diviner Chen Deng to stay overnight at his mansion in Anyi Lane.

sentences.zh: 翌日，群令吏捕登考劾，偽構吉甫陰事，密以上聞。

translations.literal: The next day Qun ordered officials to arrest Deng and examine him, falsely fabricating Jifu's secret misdeeds and privately reporting them to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Qun had his men arrest Chen and interrogate him, fabricating secret crimes to implicate Jifu, and reported the matter confidentially to the throne.

sentences.zh: 帝召登面訊之，立辯其偽。

translations.literal: The emperor summoned Deng for a face-to-face inquiry; he immediately argued that the charges were fabricated.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor summoned Chen for a personal hearing, and he at once exposed the fabrication.

sentences.zh: 憲宗怒，將誅群等，吉甫救之，出為湖南觀察使。

translations.literal: Xianzong was enraged and was about to execute Qun and the others; Jifu interceded, and Qun was sent out as Regional Inspector of Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xianzong was furious and nearly had Qun and his allies executed; Jifu interceded for them, and Qun was sent out as inspector of Hunan.

sentences.zh: 數日，改黔州刺史、黔州觀察使。

translations.literal: After several days he was transferred to Prefect of Qianzhou and Regional Inspector of Qianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Within days he was reassigned as prefect and regional inspector of Qian.

sentences.zh: 在黔中，屬大水壞其城郭，復築其城，征督溪洞諸蠻。

translations.literal: While in Qianzhong, a great flood damaged the city walls; he rebuilt the city and levied and pressed the various barbarians of the stream valleys and caves for labor.
translations.idiomatic: In Qian, a major flood destroyed the city walls; he rebuilt them and conscripted labor from the tribal peoples of the hills and streams.

sentences.zh: 程作頗急，於是，辰、錦生蠻乘險作亂，群討之不能定。

translations.literal: The work was very hurried; consequently the raw barbarians of Chen and Jin seized the difficult terrain and rebelled, and Qun could not suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: The construction was driven at punishing speed; the aboriginal tribes of Chen and Jin then seized the mountain passes and rose in revolt, and Qun failed to restore order.

sentences.zh: 六年九月，貶開州刺史。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the sixth year he was demoted to Prefect of Kaizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the sixth year he was demoted to prefect of Kaizhou.

sentences.zh: 在郡二年，改容州刺史、容管經略觀察使。

translations.literal: After two years in that prefecture he was transferred to Prefect of Rongzhou and Military Commissioner and Regional Inspector of Rongguan.
translations.idiomatic: After two years there he was appointed prefect of Rongzhou and military commissioner and regional inspector of Rongguan.

sentences.zh: 九年，詔還朝，至衡州病卒，時年五十。

translations.literal: In the ninth year an edict recalled him to court; he fell ill and died at Hengzhou, aged fifty.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he was recalled to court but fell ill and died at Hengzhou at the age of fifty.

sentences.zh: 群性狠戾，頗復恩讎，臨事不顧生死。

translations.literal: Qun's nature was fierce and perverse; he greatly repaid both kindness and enmity, and in affairs paid no heed to life or death.
translations.idiomatic: Qun was by nature fierce and unyielding, quick to repay both kindness and injury, and utterly heedless of life or death in pursuit of his aims.

sentences.zh: 是時徵入，云欲大用，人皆懼駭，聞其卒方安。

translations.literal: At that time he was summoned in, and it was said he would be greatly employed; all were frightened, and only when they heard of his death did they feel at ease.
translations.idiomatic: When he was recalled with talk of a major appointment, people were terrified; only when news of his death arrived did they breathe freely again.

sentences.zh: 二子：謙余、審余。

translations.literal: He had two sons: Qianyu and Shenyu.
translations.idiomatic: He had two sons, Qianyu and Shenyu.

sentences.zh: 群兄 常兄常，字中行，大曆十四年登進士第，居廣陵之柳楊。

translations.literal: Qun's elder brother Chang—Chang, styled Zhonghang—passed the jinshi examination in the fourteenth year of Dali and lived at Liuyang in Guangling.
translations.idiomatic: Qun's elder brother Chang, styled Zhonghang, passed the jinshi examination in the fourteenth year of Dali and made his home at Liuyang in Guangling.

sentences.zh: 結廬種樹，不求茍進，以講學著書為事，凡二十年不出。

translations.literal: He built a hut and planted trees, sought no unworthy advancement, took lecturing and writing as his occupation, and for twenty years never went out.
translations.idiomatic: He built a cottage, planted trees, and refused unworthy advancement, devoting himself to teaching and writing for twenty years without leaving home.

sentences.zh: 貞元十四年，鎮州節度使王武俊聞其賢，遣人致聘，辟為掌書記，不就。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Zhenyuan, Wang Wujun, Military Commissioner of Zhenzhou, heard of his worth, sent men to invite him, and tried to appoint him as Chief Secretary, but he did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year of Zhenyuan, Wang Wujun, military commissioner of Zhenzhou, heard of his reputation and sent envoys to recruit him as chief secretary, but Chang declined.

sentences.zh: 其年，杜佑鎮淮南，奏授校書郎，為節度參謀。

translations.literal: That same year Du You commanded Huainan, memorialized to appoint him Collator, and made him a staff strategist.
translations.idiomatic: That same year Du You, commanding Huainan, had him appointed collator and made him a strategic adviser on his staff.

sentences.zh: 元和六年，自湖南判官入為侍御史，轉水部員外郎。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Yuanhe he entered court from his post as aide in Hunan as Censor, then was transferred to Vice Director of the Ministry of Works in the Bureau of Waterways.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Yuanhe he entered court from a Hunan staff post as censor, then was promoted to vice director in the waterways bureau of the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 出為朗州刺史，歷固陵、潯陽、臨川三郡守。

translations.literal: He was sent out as Prefect of Langzhou and successively served as prefect of the three commanderies of Guling, Xunyang, and Linchuan.
translations.idiomatic: He was posted as prefect of Langzhou and later governed the three prefectures of Guling, Xunyang, and Linchuan.

sentences.zh: 入為國子祭酒，求致仕。

translations.literal: He entered court as Chancellor of the Directorate of Education and requested retirement.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to serve as chancellor of the Directorate of Education, then asked to retire.

sentences.zh: 寶曆元年卒，時年七十。

translations.literal: He died in the first year of Baoli, aged seventy.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the first year of Baoli at the age of seventy.

sentences.zh: 子弘余，會昌中為黃州刺史。

translations.literal: His son Hongyu served as Prefect of Huangzhou during Huichang.
translations.idiomatic: His son Hongyu served as prefect of Huangzhou during the Huichang era.

sentences.zh: 群兄 牟牟，字貽周，貞元二年登進士第，試秘書省校書郎、東都留守巡官。

translations.literal: Qun's elder brother Mou—Mou, styled Yizhou—passed the jinshi in the second year of Zhenyuan, was tested as Collator in the Secretariat, and served as Circuit Inspector under the Eastern Capital Protector.
translations.idiomatic: Qun's elder brother Mou, styled Yizhou, passed the jinshi in the second year of Zhenyuan, entered service as a collator in the Secretariat, and served as circuit inspector to the eastern capital protector.

sentences.zh: 歷河陽、昭義從事，檢校水部郎中，賜緋，再為留守判官。

translations.literal: He successively served as staff officer in Heyang and Zhaoyi, was Acting Chief of the Bureau of Waterways, granted the scarlet robe, and twice served as Aide to the Protector.
translations.idiomatic: He served on the staffs of Heyang and Zhaoyi, was acting chief of the waterways bureau, received the scarlet robe, and twice served as aide to a capital protector.

sentences.zh: 入為都官郎中，出為澤州刺史，入為國子祭酒。
