translations.literal: He entered court as Chief of the Bureau of Justice, was sent out as Prefect of Zezhou, and entered court again as Chancellor of the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled as chief of the bureau of justice, posted as prefect of Zezhou, then recalled again as chancellor of the Directorate of Education.

sentences.zh: 長慶二年卒，時年七十四。

translations.literal: He died in the second year of Changqing, aged seventy-four.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the second year of Changqing at the age of seventy-four.

sentences.zh: 子周余，大中年秘書監。

translations.literal: His son Zhouyu was Director of the Secretariat during the Dazhong era.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhouyu served as director of the Secretariat during the Dazhong era.

sentences.zh: 牟弟 庠牟弟庠，字胄卿，釋褐國子主簿。

translations.literal: Mou's younger brother Ku—Mou's younger brother Ku, styled Zhouqing—on first entering office was Registrar of the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: Mou's younger brother Ku, styled Zhouqing, first entered office as registrar of the Directorate of Education.

sentences.zh: 吏部侍郎韓臯出鎮武昌，辟為推官。

translations.literal: When Vice Minister of Personnel Han Gao went out to command Wuchang, he recruited Ku as Legal Examiner.
translations.idiomatic: When Han Gao, vice minister of personnel, took command at Wuchang, he recruited Ku as legal examiner on his staff.

sentences.zh: 臯移鎮浙西，奏庠為節度副使、殿中侍御史，遷澤州刺史。

translations.literal: When Gao transferred to command Zhexi, he memorialized to appoint Ku Deputy Military Commissioner and Palace Censor, then promoted him to Prefect of Zezhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Han was transferred to Zhexi, he had Ku appointed deputy commissioner and palace censor, then promoted him to prefect of Zezhou.

sentences.zh: 又為宣歙副使，除奉天令、登州刺史、東都留守判官，歷信、婺二州刺史。

translations.literal: He also served as Deputy Commissioner of Xuanxi, was appointed Magistrate of Fengtian, Prefect of Dengzhou, and Aide to the Eastern Capital Protector, and successively served as prefect of the two prefectures of Xin and Wu.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as deputy commissioner of Xuanxi, was appointed magistrate of Fengtian and prefect of Dengzhou, served as aide to the eastern capital protector, and subsequently governed Xin and Wu.

sentences.zh: 卒年六十三。

translations.literal: He died at the age of sixty-three.
translations.idiomatic: He died at sixty-three.

sentences.zh: 子繇、載。

translations.literal: His sons were You and Zai.
translations.idiomatic: He had two sons, You and Zai.

sentences.zh: 群弟 鞏鞏，字友封，元和二年登進士第。

translations.literal: Qun's younger brother Gong—Gong, styled Youfeng—passed the jinshi in the second year of Yuanhe.
translations.idiomatic: Qun's younger brother Gong, styled Youfeng, passed the jinshi in the second year of Yuanhe.

sentences.zh: 袁滋鎮滑州，辟為從事。

translations.literal: When Yuan Zi commanded Huazhou, he recruited Gong as staff officer.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Zi commanded Huazhou, he recruited Gong to his staff.

sentences.zh: 滋改荊、襄二鎮，皆從之，掌管記之任。

translations.literal: When Zi was transferred to the two circuits of Jing and Xiang, Gong followed him and held the post of chief secretary.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan was transferred to the Jing and Xiang circuits in turn, Gong followed him and served as chief secretary.

sentences.zh: 平盧薛平又辟為副使。

translations.literal: Xue Ping of Pinglu again recruited him as Deputy Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Ping of Pinglu later recruited him as deputy commissioner.

sentences.zh: 入朝，拜侍御史，歷司勛員外、刑部郎中。

translations.literal: He entered court, was appointed Censor, and successively served as Vice Director in the Bureau of Meritorious Achievements and Chief of the Bureau of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled to court, he was appointed censor and later served as vice director in the bureau of meritorious achievements and chief in the Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 元稹觀察浙東，奉為副使、檢校秘書少監，兼御史中丞，賜金紫。

translations.literal: When Yuan Zhen inspected Zhedong, he appointed Gong Deputy Commissioner, Acting Vice Director of the Secretariat, concurrently Vice Censor-in-Chief, and granted him the gold seal and purple robe.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Zhen served as inspector of eastern Zhejiang, he appointed Gong his deputy, acting vice director of the Secretariat and concurrent vice censor-in-chief, and granted him the gold seal and purple robe.

sentences.zh: 稹移鎮武昌，鞏又從之。

translations.literal: When Zhen transferred to command Wuchang, Gong again followed him.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Zhen moved to Wuchang, Gong followed him once more.

sentences.zh: 鞏能五言詩，昆仲之間，與牟詩俱為時所賞重。

translations.literal: Gong was skilled in pentasyllabic poetry; among the brothers, his poems together with Mou's were both prized by the age.
translations.idiomatic: Gong was an accomplished writer of pentasyllabic verse; among the brothers, his poetry and Mou's were both highly prized in their day.

sentences.zh: 性溫雅，多不能持論，士友言議之際，吻動而不發，白居易等目為「囁嚅翁」。

translations.literal: His nature was mild and refined; he mostly could not sustain an argument; when gentlemen and friends discussed matters, his lips would move but no words would come forth—Bai Juyi and others called him "Old Mumbler."
translations.idiomatic: Gentle and refined by nature, he rarely held his ground in debate; at gatherings of friends his lips would move but no argument would emerge, and Bai Juyi and others dubbed him "Old Mumbler."

sentences.zh: 終於鄂渚，時年六十。

translations.literal: He died at Ezhu, aged sixty.
translations.idiomatic: He died at Ezhou at the age of sixty.

sentences.zh: 子六人，景余、師裕最知名。

translations.literal: He had six sons; Jingyu and Shiyu were the most renowned.
translations.idiomatic: He had six sons; Jingyu and Shiyu were the best known.

sentences.zh: 李遜李遜，字友道，後魏申公發之後，於趙郡謂之申公房。

translations.literal: Li Xun—Li Xun—styled Youdao, a descendant of Duke Shen of Later Wei named Fa, among the Zhao commandery clans called the house of Duke Shen.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xun, styled Youdao, was descended from Fa, Duke Shen of Northern Wei; in Zhao commandery his line was known as the house of Duke Shen.

sentences.zh: 曾祖進德，太子中允。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Jinde was Principal of the Court of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Jinde had served as principal in the court of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 祖珍玉，昌明令。

translations.literal: His grandfather Zhenyu was Magistrate of Changming.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Zhenyu had been magistrate of Changming.

sentences.zh: 父震，雅州別駕。

translations.literal: His father Zhen was Vice Prefect of Yazhou.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zhen had served as vice prefect of Yazhou.

sentences.zh: 世寓於荊州之石首。

translations.literal: For generations the family sojourned at Shishou in Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: For generations the family had resided at Shishou in Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 遜登進士第，辟襄陽掌書記。

translations.literal: Xun passed the jinshi examination and was recruited as Chief Secretary at Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: Xun passed the jinshi examination and was recruited as chief secretary at Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 復從事於湖南，主其留務，頗有聲績，累拜池、濠二州刺史。

translations.literal: He again served on the staff in Hunan, managing its remaining affairs, achieved considerable reputation and merit, and was repeatedly promoted to Prefect of the two prefectures of Chi and Hao.
translations.idiomatic: He later served on the Hunan staff, managing affairs in the commander's absence, won a solid reputation, and was promoted in turn to prefect of Chi and Hao.

sentences.zh: 先是，濠州之都將楊騰，削刻士卒，州兵三千人謀殺騰。

translations.literal: Earlier, Yang Teng, chief commander of Haozhou, was harsh and scraped the soldiers; three thousand troops of the prefecture plotted to kill Teng.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Yang Teng, chief commander at Haozhou, had been harsh and exploitative toward his troops; three thousand men of the garrison plotted to kill him.

sentences.zh: 騰覺之，走揚州，家屬皆死。

translations.literal: Teng discovered it, fled to Yangzhou, and his family were all killed.
translations.idiomatic: Teng discovered the plot, fled to Yangzhou, and his entire household was slaughtered.

sentences.zh: 濠兵不自戢，因行攘剽。

translations.literal: The troops of Hao could not restrain themselves and went about plundering.
translations.idiomatic: The Haozhou soldiers lost all discipline and took to looting wherever they went.

sentences.zh: 及遜至郡，余亂未殄。

translations.literal: When Xun arrived at the prefecture, the remnants of the disturbance had not yet been extinguished.
translations.idiomatic: By the time Xun reached the prefecture, the unrest had not yet been suppressed.

sentences.zh: 徐驅其間，為陳逆順利害之勢，眾皆釋甲請罪，因以寧息。

translations.literal: He gradually drove among them, set forth for them the forces of right and wrong and advantage and harm, and all cast off their armor and asked forgiveness; thus the region was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Moving among them at a measured pace, he explained the consequences of loyalty and rebellion, and the men laid down their arms and begged forgiveness; order was thus restored.

sentences.zh: 觀察使旨限外征役，皆不從。

translations.literal: When the Regional Inspector issued orders for corvée labor beyond the prescribed limits, he did not comply with any of them.
translations.idiomatic: He refused every request from the regional inspector for labor levies beyond statutory limits.

sentences.zh: 入拜虞部郎中。

translations.literal: He entered court and was appointed Chief of the Bureau of Forestry and Craft Works.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to court and appointed chief of the bureau of forestry and craft works.

sentences.zh: 元和初，出為衢州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yuanhe he was sent out as Prefect of Quzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Yuanhe he was posted as prefect of Quzhou.

sentences.zh: 以政績殊尤，遷越州刺史，兼御史大夫、浙東都團練觀察使。

translations.literal: For exceptional administrative achievement he was transferred to Prefect of Yuezhou, concurrently Grand Censor and Regional Protector, Training Commissioner, and Inspector of Zhedong.
translations.idiomatic: For outstanding administration he was promoted to prefect of Yuezhou and concurrent grand censor, training commissioner, and regional inspector of eastern Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 先是，貞元初，皇甫政鎮浙東，嘗福建兵亂，逐觀察使吳詵。

translations.literal: Earlier, at the beginning of Zhenyuan, Huangfu Zheng commanded Zhedong; once there was a military disturbance in Fujian that drove out Regional Inspector Wu Shen.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, in the early Zhenyuan era, Huangfu Zheng had commanded eastern Zhejiang; when Fujian erupted in military unrest, Inspector Wu Shen was driven out.

sentences.zh: 政以所鎮實壓閩境，請權益兵三千，俟賊平而罷。

translations.literal: Zheng, because his command actually pressed upon the Fujian border, requested temporary augmentation of three thousand troops, to be disbanded once the rebels were pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Because his circuit bordered Fujian, Zheng requested a temporary increase of three thousand troops, to be withdrawn once order was restored.

sentences.zh: 賊平向三十年，而所益兵仍舊。

translations.literal: The rebels had been pacified for nearly thirty years, yet the augmented troops remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: Nearly thirty years after the rebellion ended, the supplemental troops were still in place.

sentences.zh: 遜視事數日，舉奏停之。

translations.literal: Within a few days of assuming office, Xun memorialized to halt them.
translations.idiomatic: Within days of taking office, Xun memorialized to have them disbanded.

sentences.zh: 遜為政以均一貧富、扶弱抑強為己任，故所至稱理。

translations.literal: Xun took as his governing principle equalizing rich and poor, supporting the weak and restraining the strong; hence wherever he went he was praised for good order.
translations.idiomatic: Xun made it his governing principle to level the gap between rich and poor and to protect the weak while restraining the powerful, and wherever he served he won praise for fair administration.

sentences.zh: 九年，入為給事中。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he entered court as Supervising Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he was recalled as supervising secretary in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 遜以舊制只日視事對群臣，遜奏論曰：「事君之義，有犯無隱。

translations.literal: Xun, because the old rule fixed a single day for conducting affairs and facing the ministers, memorialized arguing, "The principle of serving one's ruler is to remonstrate when there is offense and to conceal nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Because court audiences were restricted to fixed days, Xun memorialized: "In serving one's sovereign, the loyal subject speaks out even at risk of offense and hides nothing.

sentences.zh: 陳誠啟沃，不必擇辰。

translations.literal: Presenting honest counsel to nourish the ruler need not await a chosen day.
translations.idiomatic: Frank counsel that nourishes good governance need not wait for an appointed day.

sentences.zh: 今群臣敷奏，乃候只日，是畢歲臣下睹天顏、獻可否能幾何？」

translations.literal: Now when ministers present memorials they must wait for that single day—how much in a whole year can the officials below behold the imperial countenance and offer assent or dissent?
translations.idiomatic: Yet now officials may present memorials only on that one day—how often in a year can his servants see their sovereign's face and speak their minds?

sentences.zh: 憲宗嘉之，乃許不擇時奏對。

translations.literal: Xianzong approved this and then permitted memorials and audiences without regard to set times.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xianzong approved, and thereafter allowed officials to petition and be received without waiting for fixed audience days.

sentences.zh: 俄遷戶部侍郎。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Vice Minister of the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to vice minister of revenue.

sentences.zh: 元和十年，拜襄州刺史，充山南東道節度、觀察等使。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Yuanhe he was appointed Prefect of Xiangzhou and served as Military Commissioner, Regional Inspector, and related commissioner of the Shannan East Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year of Yuanhe he was appointed prefect of Xiangzhou and military commissioner and regional inspector of the Shannan East Circuit.

sentences.zh: 襄陽前領八郡，唐、鄧、隋在焉。

translations.literal: Xiangyang formerly administered eight commanderies; Tang, Deng, and Sui were among them.
translations.idiomatic: Xiangyang had formerly governed eight commanderies, including Tang, Deng, and Sui.

sentences.zh: 是時方討吳元濟，朝議以唐、蔡鄰接，遂以鄧隸唐州，三郡別為節制，命高霞寓領之，專俟攻討。

translations.literal: At that time they were campaigning against Wu Yuanji; court deliberation held that since Tang and Cai bordered each other, Deng was placed under Tang Prefecture, the three commanderies were separately placed under military control, Gao Xiayu was ordered to command them, and he was charged solely with awaiting the attack and suppression.
translations.idiomatic: The court was then campaigning against Wu Yuanji. Because Tang and Cai prefectures lay adjacent, Deng was placed under Tang Prefecture; the three commanderies were given a separate military commission, and Gao Xiayu was appointed to command them exclusively for the assault.

sentences.zh: 遜以五州賦餉之。

translations.literal: Xun supplied them from the tax revenues of five prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Xun supplied their provisions from the tax revenues of five prefectures.

sentences.zh: 時孫代嚴綬鎮襄陽。

translations.literal: At that time Xun replaced Yan Shou in commanding Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Xun replaced Yan Shou as military commissioner at Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 綬以八州兵討賊在唐州。

translations.literal: Shou had led troops from eight prefectures against the rebels and was at Tang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Shou was at Tang Prefecture leading troops from eight prefectures against the rebels.

sentences.zh: 既而綬以無功罷兵柄，命高霞寓代綬將兵於唐州，其襄陽軍隸於霞寓。

translations.literal: Soon Shou was stripped of military command for lack of achievement; Gao Xiayu was ordered to replace Shou and lead troops at Tang Prefecture, and the Xiangyang army was placed under Xiayu's command.
translations.idiomatic: Shou was soon removed from command for lack of results. Gao Xiayu replaced him to lead troops at Tang Prefecture, and the Xiangyang army was placed under Xiayu's authority.

sentences.zh: 軍士家口在襄州者，遜厚撫之，士卒多舍霞寓亡歸。

translations.literal: Soldiers whose families were in Xiang Prefecture—Xun treated them generously; many troops abandoned Xiayu and fled back home.
translations.idiomatic: Xun treated generously those soldiers whose families were in Xiang Prefecture, and many troops deserted Xiayu to return home.

sentences.zh: 既而霞寓為賊所敗，乃移過於遜，言供饋不時。

translations.literal: When Xiayu was afterward defeated by the rebels, he shifted the blame onto Xun, alleging that supplies had not been delivered in time.
translations.idiomatic: After Xiayu was defeated by the rebels, he blamed Xun, claiming that provisions had not arrived on schedule.

sentences.zh: 霞寓本出禁軍，內官皆佐之。

translations.literal: Xiayu had originally come from the palace guard corps, and inner-court eunuchs all assisted him.
translations.idiomatic: Xiayu had risen from the palace guard, and eunuch officials all backed him.

sentences.zh: 既貶官，中人皆言遜撓霞寓軍，所以致敗。

translations.literal: After he was demoted, eunuchs all said Xun had undermined Xiayu's army and thereby caused the defeat.
translations.idiomatic: After Xiayu was demoted, the eunuchs all blamed Xun for weakening his army and causing the defeat.

sentences.zh: 上令中使至襄州聽察曲直，奏言遜不直，乃左授太子賓客分司，又降為恩王傅。

translations.literal: The emperor sent a palace envoy to Xiang Prefecture to investigate right and wrong; the report said Xun was in the wrong, and he was transferred to the left as Senior Adviser to the Heir Apparent in a nominal post, then demoted to Tutor to the Prince of En.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor dispatched a palace envoy to Xiang Prefecture to adjudicate the dispute. The envoy reported that Xun was at fault, and Xun was demoted to senior adviser to the heir apparent with nominal duties, then further reduced to tutor to the Prince of En.

sentences.zh: 十三年，李師道效順，命遜為左散騎常侍，馳赴東平諭之。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, when Li Shidao submitted to the throne, Xun was appointed Left Regular Attendant of the Palace Secretariat and galloped to Dongping to instruct him.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year, when Li Shidao submitted, Xun was appointed left regular attendant and dispatched post-haste to Dongping to persuade him.

sentences.zh: 師道得詔意動，即請效順，旋為其下所惑而止。

translations.literal: Shidao, upon receiving the edict, was moved and immediately asked to submit; he was soon turned back by being misled by his subordinates.
translations.idiomatic: Shidao was moved on receiving the edict and at once offered to submit, but was soon dissuaded by his subordinates and changed his mind.

sentences.zh: 遜還，未幾，除京兆尹，改國子祭酒。

translations.literal: Xun returned; before long he was appointed Magistrate of the Capital, then transferred to Chancellor of the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: Xun returned and was soon made magistrate of the capital, then chancellor of the Directorate of Education.

sentences.zh: 十四年，拜許州刺史，充忠武節度、陳許溵蔡等州觀察處置等使。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he was appointed Prefect of Xuzhou and served as Military Commissioner of Zhongwu, Regional Inspector and Disposition Commissioner of Chen, Xu, Wen, Cai, and related prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year he was appointed prefect of Xuzhou and military commissioner of Zhongwu and regional inspector of Chen, Xu, Wen, Cai, and related prefectures.

sentences.zh: 是時，新罹兵戰，難遽完緝。

translations.literal: At that time the region had newly suffered warfare and could not quickly be fully restored to order.
translations.idiomatic: The region had just emerged from war and could not quickly be fully pacified.

sentences.zh: 及遜至，集大軍與之約束，嚴具示賞罰必信，號令數百言，士皆感悅。

translations.literal: When Xun arrived, he assembled the great army and imposed discipline upon them, strictly showing that rewards and punishments would be kept, issuing orders of several hundred words; the troops were all moved and pleased.
translations.idiomatic: When Xun arrived, he assembled the army, imposed strict discipline, and delivered a proclamation several hundred words long declaring that rewards and punishments would be faithfully enforced. The troops were deeply impressed.

sentences.zh: 長慶元年，幽、鎮繼亂。

translations.literal: In the first year of Changqing, Youzhou and Zhenzhou rebelled in succession.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Changqing, the circuits of Youzhou and Zhenzhou rebelled in turn.

sentences.zh: 遜請身先討賊，不許。

translations.literal: Xun requested to take the lead in attacking the rebels; permission was denied.
translations.idiomatic: Xun asked to lead the campaign personally, but the request was denied.

sentences.zh: 但命以兵一萬，會於行營。

translations.literal: He was only ordered to send ten thousand troops to rendezvous at the field headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered instead to dispatch ten thousand troops to join the field headquarters.

sentences.zh: 遜奉詔，即日發兵，故先諸軍而至，由是進位檢校吏部尚書。

translations.literal: Xun obeyed the edict and mobilized troops that same day; therefore he arrived before the other armies and was promoted to Acting Minister of the Ministry of Civil Office.
translations.idiomatic: Xun obeyed at once and marched his troops out the same day, arriving ahead of the other armies. For this he was promoted to acting minister of civil appointments.

sentences.zh: 尋改鳳翔節度使，行至京師，以疾陳乞，改刑部尚書。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Military Commissioner of Fengxiang; when he reached the capital he pleaded illness and was changed to Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon transferred to military commissioner of Fengxiang, but upon reaching the capital he pleaded illness and was reassigned as minister of justice.

sentences.zh: 長慶三年正月卒，年六十三，廢朝一日，贈右僕射。

translations.literal: In the first month of the third year of Changqing he died, aged sixty-three; court mourning was suspended for one day, and he was posthumously granted the right vice grand councilor.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the first month of the third year of Changqing, aged sixty-three. Court audiences were suspended for one day, and he was posthumously granted right vice grand councilor.

sentences.zh: 遜幼孤，寓居江陵。

translations.literal: Xun was orphaned in youth and resided in Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned in youth, Xun lived in Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 與其弟建，皆安貧苦，易衣並食，講習不倦。

translations.literal: He and his younger brother Jian both were content with poverty and hardship, shared clothes and food, and studied without wearying.
translations.idiomatic: He and his younger brother Jian lived contentedly in poverty, sharing clothes and meals and studying tirelessly together.

sentences.zh: 遜兄造，知二弟賢，日為營丐，成其誌業。

translations.literal: Xun's elder brother Zao, knowing the two younger brothers were worthy, daily sought provisions for them to fulfill their aims and studies.
translations.idiomatic: Their elder brother Zao, recognizing his two younger brothers' talent, worked daily to provide for them so they could pursue their ambitions.

sentences.zh: 建先遜一年卒。

translations.literal: Jian died one year before Xun.
translations.idiomatic: Jian died one year before Xun.

sentences.zh: 兄弟同致休顯，士君子多之。

translations.literal: The brothers alike attained honor and eminence; gentlemen greatly praised them.
translations.idiomatic: The brothers alike achieved distinction, and men of worth widely praised them.

sentences.zh: 謚曰恭肅。

translations.literal: His posthumous title was Gongsu (Respectful and Solemn).
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously titled Gongsu (Respectful and Solemn).

sentences.zh: 造早卒。

translations.literal: Zao died early.
translations.idiomatic: Zao died young.

sentences.zh: 遜弟 建建，字杓直，家素清貧，無舊業。

translations.literal: Xun's younger brother Jian, courtesy name Shaozhi, came from a family long poor and upright, with no inherited estate.
translations.idiomatic: Xun's younger brother Jian, courtesy name Shaozhi, came from a family of long-standing poverty and integrity, with no ancestral property.

sentences.zh: 與兄造、遜於荊南躬耕致養，嗜學力文。

translations.literal: With his elder brothers Zao and Xun he personally tilled the fields in southern Jing to support their parents, and avidly studied and worked at letters.
translations.idiomatic: With his brothers Zao and Xun he farmed in southern Jing to support their parents, studying and writing with tireless devotion.

sentences.zh: 舉進士，選授秘書省校書郎。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination and was selected and appointed Collator in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination and was appointed collator in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 德宗聞其名，用為右拾遺、翰林學士。

translations.literal: Dezong heard his name and employed him as Right Remonstrating Censor and Hanlin Academician.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Dezong heard of him and appointed him right remonstrating censor and Hanlin academician.

sentences.zh: 元和六年，坐事罷職，降詹事府司直。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Yuanhe he was dismissed from office because of an offense and demoted to Directing Secretary in the Household of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Yuanhe he was dismissed for an offense and demoted to directing secretary in the heir apparent's household.

sentences.zh: 高郢為御史大夫，奏為殿中侍御史，遷兵部郎中、知制誥。

translations.literal: When Gao Ying was Censor-in-Chief, he memorialized to appoint Jian Attending Censor within the Palace; he was transferred to Director in the Ministry of War and put in charge of drafting edicts.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Ying became censor-in-chief, he had Jian appointed attending censor within the palace. Jian was then promoted to director in the Ministry of War and put in charge of drafting edicts.

sentences.zh: 自以草詔思遲，不願司文翰，改京兆尹。

translations.literal: He considered himself slow in composing edicts and did not wish to oversee literary drafts, and so was transferred to Magistrate of the Capital.
translations.idiomatic: Finding himself slow at drafting edicts, he preferred not to oversee literary composition and was transferred to magistrate of the capital.

sentences.zh: 與宰相韋貫之友善。

translations.literal: He was on friendly terms with Grand Councilor Wei Guanzhi.
translations.idiomatic: He was on friendly terms with Grand Councilor Wei Guanzhi.

sentences.zh: 貫之罷相，建亦出為澧州刺史。

translations.literal: When Guanzhi was removed as chancellor, Jian was also sent out as Prefect of Li Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When Guanzhi was removed from the chancellorship, Jian was also sent out as prefect of Li Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 征拜太常少卿，尋以本官知禮部貢舉。

translations.literal: He was summoned and appointed Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, and soon, while retaining that office, put in charge of the Ministry of Rites civil service examinations.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled as vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and soon given charge of the civil service examinations in the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 建取舍非其人，又惑於請托，故其年選士不精，坐罰俸料。

translations.literal: Jian in selecting and rejecting men chose those who were not suitable, and was also swayed by solicitations; therefore that year his selection of scholars was not refined, and he was penalized by a fine on his salary.
translations.idiomatic: Jian's selections were unsuitable and were swayed by favor-seeking, so that year's examination produced inferior candidates, and he was fined a portion of his salary.

sentences.zh: 明年，除禮部侍郎，竟以人情不洽，改為刑部。

translations.literal: The next year he was appointed Vice Minister of Rites, but because he could not harmonize with public sentiment, he was transferred to the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was made vice minister of rites, but failing to get along with colleagues, he was transferred to the Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 建名位雖顯，以廉儉自處，家不理垣屋，士友推之。

translations.literal: Though Jian's fame and rank were eminent, he maintained himself in integrity and frugality; at home he did not repair walls and roof, and gentleman friends praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Though Jian's rank was high, he lived modestly and frugally, never repairing his house, and earned praise from friends for it.

sentences.zh: 長慶二年二月卒，贈工部尚書。

translations.literal: In the second month of the second year of Changqing he died and was posthumously granted Minister of Public Works.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the second month of the second year of Changqing and was posthumously granted minister of public works.

sentences.zh: 三子：訥、恪、樸。

translations.literal: Three sons: Ne, Ke, and Pu.
translations.idiomatic: He had three sons: Ne, Ke, and Pu.

sentences.zh: 訥最知名，官至華州刺史、檢校尚書右僕射。

translations.literal: Ne was most renowned; he reached the offices of Prefect of Hua Prefecture and Acting Right Vice Minister of the Ministry of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Ne was the most famous, rising to prefect of Hua Prefecture and acting right vice minister of state affairs.

sentences.zh: 薛戎薛戎，字元夫，河中寶鼎人。

translations.literal: Xue Rong—Xue Rong—courtesy name Yuanfu, was a native of Baoding in Hezhong.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Rong, courtesy name Yuanfu, was a native of Baoding in Hezhong.

sentences.zh: 少有學術，不求聞達，居於毗陵之陽羨山。

translations.literal: From youth he had learning and scholarship but did not seek fame and advancement; he lived on Yangxian Mountain in Piling.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he was learned but sought no fame, living on Yangxian Mountain in Piling.

sentences.zh: 年余四十，不易其操。

translations.literal: Past the age of forty, he did not change his principles.
translations.idiomatic: Even past forty he held to his principles unchanged.

sentences.zh: 江西觀察使李衡辟為從事，使者三返方應。

translations.literal: Li Heng, Regional Inspector of Jiangxi, recruited him as a staff officer; the messenger returned three times before he consented.
translations.idiomatic: Li Heng, regional inspector of Jiangxi, recruited him as a staff officer, but he refused until the envoy had come three times.

sentences.zh: 故相齊映代衡，又留署職，府罷歸山。

translations.literal: The former chancellor Qi Ying replaced Heng and again retained him in an office; when the prefecture was disbanded he returned to the mountains.
translations.idiomatic: When the former chancellor Qi Ying replaced Heng, Rong was retained on staff again; when the commission ended he returned to his mountain retreat.

sentences.zh: 福建觀察使柳冕表為從事，累月，轉殿中侍御史。

translations.literal: Liu Mian, Regional Inspector of Fujian, recommended him as a staff officer; after several months he was transferred to Attending Censor within the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Mian, regional inspector of Fujian, recommended him as a staff officer, and after several months he was promoted to attending censor within the palace.

sentences.zh: 會泉州闕刺史，冕署戎權領州事。

translations.literal: When Quanzhou lacked a prefect, Mian deputized Rong to provisionally manage the prefecture's affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Quanzhou had no prefect, Mian deputized Rong to administer the prefecture in an acting capacity.

sentences.zh: 是時，姚南仲節制鄭滑，從事馬總以其道直為監軍使誣奏，貶泉州別駕。

translations.literal: At that time Yao Nanzhong commanded Zheng and Hua; his staff officer Ma Zong, because of his upright conduct, was slanderously memorialized by the army supervisory commissioner and demoted to Vice Prefect of Quanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Yao Nanzhong commanded Zheng and Hua circuits. His staff officer Ma Zong, for his upright character, was falsely accused by the army supervisory commissioner and demoted to vice prefect of Quanzhou.

sentences.zh: 冕附會權勢，欲構成總罪，使戎按問曲成之。

translations.literal: Mian allied with powerful interests and wished to fabricate Zong's guilt, sending Rong to conduct an investigation and neatly complete the case.
translations.idiomatic: Mian curried favor with the powerful and sought to fabricate charges against Zong, ordering Rong to investigate and frame the case.

sentences.zh: 戎以總無辜，不從冕意，別白其狀。

translations.literal: Rong, holding that Zong was innocent, did not follow Mian's intent and separately clarified the true circumstances.
translations.idiomatic: Convinced of Zong's innocence, Rong refused to cooperate and filed a separate report stating the facts.

sentences.zh: 戎還自泉州，冕盛氣據衙而見賓客。

translations.literal: When Rong returned from Quanzhou, Mian, in full fury, occupied the hall of office to receive guests.
translations.idiomatic: When Rong returned from Quanzhou, Mian received guests in the yamen with deliberate arrogance.

sentences.zh: 戎遂歷東廂從容而入。

translations.literal: Rong then passed through the east wing and entered at ease.
translations.idiomatic: Rong entered calmly through the east wing.

sentences.zh: 冕度勢未可屈，徐起以見，一揖而退。

translations.literal: Mian, estimating that he could not bend him, slowly rose to receive him, bowed once, and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing he could not intimidate Rong, Mian rose slowly to greet him, exchanged a single bow, and let him go.

sentences.zh: 又構其罪以狀聞，置戎於佛寺，環以武夫，恣其侵辱，如是累月，誘令成總之罪。

translations.literal: He then fabricated charges against him and reported them in a memorial, placing Rong in a Buddhist temple surrounded by armed men who freely humiliated him; thus for many months he tried to induce Rong to confirm Zong's guilt.
translations.idiomatic: Mian then fabricated charges and reported them to the throne, confining Rong in a Buddhist temple ringed with armed thugs who abused him at will. For months he tried to coerce Rong into implicating Zong.

sentences.zh: 操心如一，竟不動搖。

translations.literal: Rong's heart and conduct remained one and the same; in the end he did not waver.
translations.idiomatic: Rong held firm throughout and never yielded.

sentences.zh: 杜佑鎮淮南，知戎之冤，乃上其表，發書諭冕，戎難方解，遂辭職寓居於江湖間。

translations.literal: Du You commanded Huainan, knew of Rong's injustice, memorialized with his petition, and sent a letter admonishing Mian; only then was Rong's ordeal resolved, whereupon he resigned and took up residence among the rivers and lakes.
translations.idiomatic: Du You, military commissioner of Huainan, learned of Rong's injustice, forwarded his petition to the throne, and wrote to reprimand Mian. Only then was Rong released. He resigned and lived in seclusion along the waterways.

sentences.zh: 後閻濟美為福建觀察使，備聞其事，奏充副使。

translations.literal: Later Yan Jimei served as Regional Inspector of Fujian, having fully heard of this affair, and memorialized to appoint Rong deputy commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Yan Jimei became regional inspector of Fujian, having heard the full story, he had Rong appointed his deputy.

sentences.zh: 又隨濟美移鎮浙東，改侍御史，入拜刑部員外郎。

translations.literal: He again followed Jimei when Jimei was transferred to command Zhedong, was changed to Attending Censor, and entered court as Assistant in the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: When Jimei moved to Zhedong, Rong followed him, was promoted to attending censor, and entered court as assistant minister of justice.

sentences.zh: 出為河南令，累改衢、湖、常三州刺史，遷浙東觀察使。

translations.literal: He went out as Magistrate of Henan, was successively transferred to Prefect of Qu, Hu, and Chang prefectures, and was promoted to Regional Inspector of Zhedong.
translations.idiomatic: He served as magistrate of Henan, then successively as prefect of Qu, Hu, and Chang, and was finally promoted to regional inspector of Zhedong.

sentences.zh: 所蒞皆以政績聞。

translations.literal: Wherever he held office, he was known for administrative achievement.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever he served, he was noted for effective governance.

sentences.zh: 居數歲，以疾辭官。

translations.literal: After several years he resigned on grounds of illness.
translations.idiomatic: After several years he resigned due to illness.

sentences.zh: 長慶元年十月卒，贈左散騎常侍。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the first year of Changqing he died and was posthumously granted Left Regular Attendant of the Palace Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the tenth month of the first year of Changqing and was posthumously granted left regular attendant.

sentences.zh: 戎檢身處約，不務虛名。

translations.literal: Rong restrained himself and lived in modesty, not pursuing empty fame.
translations.idiomatic: Rong lived modestly and shunned hollow reputation.

sentences.zh: 俸入之余，散於宗族。

translations.literal: What remained of his salary he distributed among his clan.
translations.idiomatic: He gave away his salary beyond his own needs to his extended family.

sentences.zh: 身歿之後，人無譏焉。

translations.literal: After his death no one criticized him.
translations.idiomatic: After his death no one found fault with him.

sentences.zh: 兄弟五人，季弟放最知名。

translations.literal: Among five brothers, the youngest, Fang, was most renowned.
translations.idiomatic: Of five brothers, the youngest, Fang, was the most famous.

sentences.zh: 放登進士第，性端厚寡言，於是非不甚系意。

translations.literal: Fang passed the jinshi examination; his nature was upright, substantial, and sparing of speech, and he did not greatly fix his mind on right and wrong disputes.
translations.idiomatic: Fang passed the jinshi examination. Upright, steady, and reticent, he did not dwell much on partisan disputes.

sentences.zh: 累佐籓府，蒞事幹敏。

translations.literal: He repeatedly assisted regional headquarters; in handling affairs he was capable and alert.
translations.idiomatic: He served repeatedly on regional staffs and handled affairs with alert competence.

sentences.zh: 官至試大理評事，擢拜右拾遺，轉補闕，歷水部、兵部二員外，遷兵部郎中。

translations.literal: He reached the office of Probationary Evaluator of the Court of Judicial Review; he was elevated and appointed Right Remonstrating Censor, transferred to Supplementing Censor, passed through the two assistant posts in the Ministries of Public Works and War, and was promoted to Director in the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to probationary evaluator of the Court of Judicial Review, was appointed right remonstrating censor, then supplemental censor, served as assistant in the ministries of public works and war, and was promoted to director in the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 遇憲宗以儲皇好書，求端士輔導經義，選充皇太子侍讀。

translations.literal: When Xianzong found the heir apparent fond of books and sought upright scholars to instruct him in the classics, Fang was selected and appointed Reader-in-Waiting to the Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xianzong found the crown prince fond of books and sought upright scholars to instruct him in the classics, Fang was chosen as reader-in-waiting to the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 及穆宗嗣位，未聽政間，放多在左右，密參機命。

translations.literal: When Muzong succeeded to the throne, during the interval before he took up governance, Fang was often at his side, secretly participating in confidential orders.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Muzong succeeded to the throne, Fang was often at his side during the period before formal audiences resumed, secretly advising on affairs of state.

sentences.zh: 穆宗常謂放曰：「小子初承大寶，懼不克荷，先生宜為相，以匡不逮。」

translations.literal: Muzong often said to Fang: "This young man has newly received the great treasure and fears he cannot bear it; you, sir, ought to serve as chancellor to correct my deficiencies."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Muzong often told Fang: "I have only just received the throne and fear I cannot bear its weight. You, sir, should serve as chancellor to remedy my shortcomings.

sentences.zh: 放叩頭曰：「臣實庸淺，獲侍冕旒，固不足猥塵大位。

translations.literal: Fang kowtowed and said: "Your servant is truly shallow and mediocre; to have been granted attendance upon the imperial cap and tassels is already more than enough—I am not fit to sully so great a station.
translations.idiomatic: Fang kowtowed and said: "I am truly unworthy. To serve at Your Majesty's side is honor enough; I am far too base to occupy so exalted a post.

sentences.zh: 輔弼之任，自有賢能。」

translations.literal: The duty of assisting and supporting belongs properly to the worthy and capable."
translations.idiomatic: The work of governance belongs to those truly worthy and able.

sentences.zh: 其言無矯飾，皆此類也。

translations.literal: His words were without artificial adornment; all were of this kind.
translations.idiomatic: His words were never affected; all were like this.

sentences.zh: 穆宗深嘉其誠，因召對思政殿，賜以金紫之服。

translations.literal: Muzong deeply praised his sincerity, therefore summoned him for audience in the Hall of Governance Through Reflecting on Government, and bestowed upon him robes of gold and purple.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Muzong deeply appreciated his sincerity, summoned him to the Hall of Governance Through Reflecting on Government, and granted him gold-and-purple robes.

sentences.zh: 轉工部侍郎、集賢學士。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Vice Minister of Public Works and Academician of the Court of Assembled Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to vice minister of public works and academician of the Court of Assembled Worthies.

sentences.zh: 雖任非峻切，而恩顧轉隆。

translations.literal: Though his office was not lofty and pressing, imperial favor toward him grew ever greater.
translations.idiomatic: Though his post was not the highest, imperial favor toward him steadily increased.

sentences.zh: 轉刑部侍郎，職如故。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Vice Minister of Justice; his duties remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to vice minister of justice while retaining his previous duties.

sentences.zh: 穆宗常謂侍臣曰：「朕欲習學經史，何先？」

translations.literal: Muzong often said to his attending ministers: "I wish to study the classics and histories—what should come first?"
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Muzong often asked his ministers: "I wish to study the classics and histories. Where should I begin?

sentences.zh: 放對曰：「經者，先聖之至言，仲尼之所發明，皆天人之極致，誠萬代不刊之典也。

translations.literal: Fang replied: "The classics are the supreme words of the ancient sages, elucidated by Confucius; all are the utmost reach of Heaven and man—truly canons for ten thousand generations that shall not be effaced.
translations.idiomatic: Fang replied: "The classics are the supreme teachings of the ancient sages, elucidated by Confucius. They represent the highest wisdom of Heaven and man—indeed, canons for all ages that cannot be superseded.

sentences.zh: 史記前代成敗得失之跡，亦足鑒其興亡。

translations.literal: Histories record the tracks of success and failure, gain and loss, of former ages and are also sufficient to mirror their rise and fall.
translations.idiomatic: Histories record the successes and failures of earlier ages and offer lessons in the rise and fall of dynasties.

sentences.zh: 然得失相參，是非無準的，固不可為經典比也。」

translations.literal: Yet gain and loss are intermixed, right and wrong have no fixed standard, and truly they cannot be compared with the classics."
translations.idiomatic: Yet they mingle success with failure and offer no fixed standard of right and wrong. They cannot be ranked with the classics.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「《六經》所尚不一，誌學之士，白首不能盡通，如何得其要？」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "The Six Classics each esteem different things; scholars who aspire to learning cannot fully master them even with white hair—how can one grasp their essentials?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "The Six Classics each emphasize different things. Even scholars who study all their lives cannot master them fully. How may one grasp their essentials?

sentences.zh: 對曰：「《論語》者《六經》之菁華，《孝經》者人倫之本。

translations.literal: He replied: "The Analects are the essence of the Six Classics; the Classic of Filial Piety is the root of human relations.
translations.idiomatic: He replied: "The Analects are the essence of the Six Classics, and the Classic of Filial Piety is the foundation of human relations.

sentences.zh: 窮理執要，真可謂聖人至言。

translations.literal: Exhausting principle and grasping essentials—they may truly be called the supreme words of the sages.
translations.idiomatic: To exhaust principle and grasp essentials—these are truly the supreme words of the sages.

sentences.zh: 是以漢朝《論語》首列學官，光武令虎賁之士皆習《孝經》，玄宗親為《孝經》註解，皆使當時大理，四海乂寧。

translations.literal: Therefore in the Han dynasty the Analects were first placed among the academy officials; Emperor Guangwu ordered the tiger-guard warriors all to study the Classic of Filial Piety; Emperor Xuanzong personally annotated the Classic of Filial Piety—all brought great order in their time, and the four seas were at peace.
translations.idiomatic: That is why the Han placed the Analects first among official curricula, why Emperor Guangwu ordered his tiger guards to study the Classic of Filial Piety, and why Emperor Xuanzong personally annotated it—all ages that did so enjoyed great order and peace throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 蓋人知孝慈，氣感和樂之所致也。」

translations.literal: This is because when people know filial piety and compassion, the harmony of vital breath and feeling produces concord and joy."
translations.idiomatic: When people understand filial piety and compassion, the harmony of spirit itself brings peace and joy.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「聖人以孝為至德要道，其信然乎！」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "The sages take filial piety as the utmost virtue and essential way—is this not truly so!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "The sages call filial piety the highest virtue and the essential path—is this not indeed so!

sentences.zh: 轉兵部侍郎、禮部尚書，判院事。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Vice Minister of War and Minister of Rites, with charge of the Academy's affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to vice minister of war and minister of rites, with charge of the Directorate of Education.

sentences.zh: 放閨門之內，尤推孝睦，孤孀百口，家貧每不給贍，常苦俸薄。

translations.literal: Within Fang's household he especially promoted filial piety and harmony; widows and orphans numbered a hundred mouths, the family was poor and often could not provide support, and he constantly suffered from a thin salary.
translations.idiomatic: Within his household Fang was especially devoted to filial piety and harmony. With a hundred widows and orphans under his roof, the family was often destitute, and his salary never sufficed.

sentences.zh: 放因召對，懇求外任。

translations.literal: Fang, upon being summoned for audience, earnestly requested an outside appointment.
translations.idiomatic: At an imperial audience Fang earnestly requested a provincial appointment.

sentences.zh: 其時偶以節制無闕，乃授以廉問。

translations.literal: At that time, as it happened no military commission was vacant, he was granted a regional inspection post.
translations.idiomatic: As no military commission happened to be open, he was given a regional inspectorship.

sentences.zh: 及鎮江西，惟用清潔為理，一方之人，至今思之。

translations.literal: When he governed Jiangxi, he used integrity and cleanliness alone as his governing principle; the people of that region remember him to this day.
translations.idiomatic: When he governed Jiangxi he ruled with integrity and restraint alone, and the people there remember him to this day.

sentences.zh: 寶歷元年，卒於江西觀察使，廢朝一日。

translations.literal: In the first year of Baoli he died while serving as Regional Inspector of Jiangxi; the court suspended audiences for one day.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Baoli he died in office as regional inspector of Jiangxi, and the court suspended court for one day in mourning.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰史臣曰：穆秘監之剛正不奪，如寒松倚巖，千丈勁節。

translations.literal: The historiographer says: Vice Director of the Palace Library Mu's upright firmness that could not be bent away was like a cold pine leaning on a cliff—a thousand zhang of sturdy joints.
translations.idiomatic: The historiographer writes: Mu, vice director of the Palace Library, was so upright and unyielding that he seemed a winter pine clinging to a cliff, every branch stiff with integrity.

sentences.zh: 而竇容州之敢決，如鷙鳥逐雀，英氣動人，巖穴之流，罕能及此。

translations.literal: Dou of Rongzhou's daring decisiveness was like a fierce bird chasing sparrows, stirring heroic spirit; men of caves and valleys could rarely match this.
translations.idiomatic: Dou of Rongzhou acted with the bold decisiveness of a hawk stooping on sparrows, his heroic spirit moving all who met him—recluses and hermits could seldom equal him.

sentences.zh: 然矯激過當，君子不為。

translations.literal: Yet excessive provocation and extremity are not what gentlemen do.
translations.idiomatic: Yet to goad and provoke beyond measure is not the way of a gentleman.

sentences.zh: 如塤如篪，不通不介，士行之美，崔氏諸子有焉。

translations.literal: Harmonious as the xun and chi flutes, neither coarse nor aloof—the beauty of scholarly conduct was found in the sons of the Cui clan.
translations.idiomatic: Harmonious as paired flutes, neither crude nor distant in manner—the finest scholar-official conduct belonged to the sons of the Cui clan.

sentences.zh: 建、遜之貞方，戎、放之道義，元和已來，稱為令族，宜哉！

translations.literal: Jian and Xun's rectitude, Rong and Fang's moral principle—since Yuanhe they have been called an exemplary clan, as they should be!
translations.idiomatic: Jian and Xun were models of rectitude, Rong and Fang of moral principle; since the Yuanhe era they have been hailed as an exemplary clan—and rightly so.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：穆之贊、質，竇之常、群，跡參時傑，氣爽人文。

translations.literal: Praise says: Mu's Zan and Zhi, Dou's Chang and Qun—their tracks joined the outstanding men of the age, their spirit refreshed human culture.
translations.idiomatic: In praise: Mu's Zan and Zhi, Dou's Chang and Qun walked among the great men of their age and breathed fresh life into the culture of their time.

sentences.zh: 二李英英，四崔濟濟。

translations.literal: The two Lis, splendid; the four Cuis, abundant.
translations.idiomatic: The two Lis, each outstanding; the four Cuis, a host of talent.

sentences.zh: 薛氏三門，難兄難弟。

translations.literal: Three branches of the Xue clan—brothers each as worthy as the other.
translations.idiomatic: Three branches of the Xue clan—brothers every one the equal of the next.
